creatures.label: Colorful cobra
creatures.desc: A large predatory snake. Cobras can be highly aggressive if provoked, and their bite injects toxic venom into the victim.

creatures.label: dromedary
creatures.desc:
A large land mammal adapted to arid environments. Domesticated since ancient times, its leather is exceptionally good at insulating against the desert heat, and its milk is quite nourishing. It can be used as a pack animal and mount, but its bouncing gait makes it slower to ride than a horse.

By storing water in its large humps and reclaiming moisture from its breath as it exhales, it can go week

creatures.label: iguana
creatures.desc:
These large lizards normally feed on plant matter. However, when angered, their tough hide and sharp claws make them quite dangerous.

Resting iguanas hold their heads high, giving them an amusing 'proud' look. But they're not proud; they're just trying to see predators so they don't get eaten.

creatures.label: vulture
creatures.desc: Scavengers with strong beaks and broad wings. Their strong stomach acid allows them to eat rotting corpses.

creatures.label: chinchilla
creatures.desc: A small, nimble rodent. Its fur is softer than just about anything in the universe, making it very valuable as a trade good.

creatures.label: Colorful lava snail
creatures.desc: A large slow-moving mollusk. Originating from the volcanic planet Nuchandus, lava snails were bred as farm animals. Their skin secretes a thick slime that protects them from extreme temperatures.

creatures.label: gizka
creatures.desc: Whatever their native world, their extraordinary reproduction rate led to a fair amount of gizka on many worlds, even including uncharted planets such as Lehon, finding their way from the wreckage of crashed starships. It has been alternatively postulated that they came from that planet originally, spreading along with the Infinite Empire. Their exponential population growth led to them being cons

creatures.label: sonar rabbit
creatures.desc: The echolocation ability of this rabbit has enabled it to survive even in pitch-black environments. It tends to feed on and make its home within the smaller fungi of the underground.

creatures.label: swarmlings
creatures.desc: The juvenile form of insectoids, swarmlings are more or less harmless, slow and easy to kill. After some time has passed, they undergo a metamorphosis, forming a cocoon from which an adult insectoid will emerge. There is no way to tell what kind of insect will crawl out of its cocoon.

creatures.label: worrt
creatures.desc: The Worrt was an amphibious creature native to the planet Tatooine, though they could also be found on other worlds (including Nal Hutta and Phaeda). Worrts were omnivorous, but was also known to attempt to eat rocks and metal objects. They used their long, prehensile tongue to catch smaller prey, such as gorgs, but were known to also attack creatures larger than itself.

creatures.desc: A cactus genetically modified to give it sentience. The first iteration of this creature was supposed to be a stationary tactical deterrent (the Whip Cactus), but having no intelligence or mobility crippled its effectiveness. creatures.label: terrestrial octopus
creatures.desc: This land-dwelling octopus has somehow adapted to being fully amphibious, able to survive for long periods out of the water. Much like other octopi, it predates on anything small enough.

creatures.label: blood shrimp

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
A smaller relative of the Raptor Shrimp, the Blood Shrimp lacks the impressive regenerative abilities of its larger counterpart. Blood Shrimp compensate this disadvantage by being faster and more agile.

Blood Shrimps are vampiric, feeding on blood and being able to regenerate their wounds when drinking the blood of live animals.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com

creatures.desc: The Razorjack is a very aggressive and adaptable creature with a strange body plan: a dual-jawed mouth that leads to two separate but intertwined digestive systems, each of them adapted to consume different types of food. creatures.label: diggerpede
creatures.desc:
The predatory diggerpede is found below the desert surface, burrowing in the sand and soil faster than most can run. It hunts anything it can lay its mandibles on when it hungers.

Despite being similar to other arthropods, it gives live birth rather than lay eggs.

creatures.label: boomcat

evidence.why: produces <VCHE_Deepchem> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
Combining the frequent nuzzling of a cat and the deepchem production of a primary boomalope hybrid is surely in no way going to end badly. Better not to ignore them should they complain loudly about wanting dinner.

A boomalope hybrid with recessive feline genes. They make for an interesting companion for those who desire chemfuel production but also want to be able to cuddle said creatures. They

creatures.label: hawk-bat
creatures.desc: Hawk-bats were predatory reptavians with a curved beak and leathery wings that could be found on urbanized worlds like Coruscant and Taris. To get on a hawk-bat's bad side could be very dangerous. As a result, very few lived in captivity. Though they favored granite slugs, hawk-bats would feed on almost anything smaller than themselves. When they hatched from their eggs, young hawk-bats had scaly

creatures.label: lynx
creatures.desc: A wildcat larger than a housecat, but smaller than a cougar. Lynxes survive on a diet of small birds and animals. Their very warm fur keeps them safe from the brutally cold temperatures of their frozen territories.

creatures.label: teratogenic originator
creatures.desc:
This amorphous, flesh coloured, translucent creature seems to lack everything but the most basic instincts, moving around slowly and sometimes devouring any plant it comes in contact with, incorporating it into its cytoplasm. There are some chunks of seemingly normal flesh floating inside it.

Teratogenic Originators are basically an enormous clonal colony of pluripotent stem cells, capable of dif

creatures.label: Colorful bullfrog
creatures.desc: A large frog known for its loud croak. Bullfrog legs are a delicacy on some planets.

creatures.label: colossus toad
creatures.desc: A massive frog bioengineered for industrial farms. While safe to eat, its thick skin secretes an unpleasant slime.

creatures.label: Thrumba toad
creatures.desc: A massive frog bioengineered for war. While safe to eat, its thick skin secretes an unpleasant slime.

creatures.label: Colorful tortoise
creatures.desc: This heavily armored land-dwelling reptile is known for its slow moving speed and surprisingly vicious bite. Because of its natural armor, it is tough to kill and can do serious damage during drawn-out melee fights.

creatures.label: Colorful monitor lizard
creatures.desc: A large venomous lizard. They secrete toxins from venom glands in their lower jaw to neutralize their prey.

creatures.label: squirrel
creatures.desc: One of the many hardy rodent species that follows humankind everywhere it spreads. Squirrels are distinguished by their bushy tails, which they use as umbrellas in bad weather.

creatures.label: red fox
creatures.desc: A small solitary canine evolved for hunting small prey in temperate climates. Chicken farmers hate foxes because of their ability to destroy a whole coop in minutes.

creatures.label: goat
creatures.desc: Naturally curious about the world, goats are among the friendliest domesticated creature bred by mankind.

creatures.label: deer
creatures.desc: A medium-sized herding herbivore which prefers to live in mixed forests and plains. Deer are very quick.

creatures.label: aerofleet

evidence.why: produces <AA_BlueGel> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
A small, floating gelatinous creature. Propelled by the hydrogen it collects from water and various plant matter, these squishy creatures wander the lands, aimlessly bouncing off objects in their path. One of the few rare creatures around here that strangely isn’t out for human blood. Well, isn’t that nice?

Aerofleets are genderless, and reproduce by strobilation, a form of asexual reproduction.

creatures.label: Protovermes
creatures.desc:

A blood-red cynodont that is peaceful unless disturbed. Its modern decendants are still alive on the rim to this day. Interestingly enough the ability to ignite itself after death remains even through normal genome restoration means, implying that the rim underwent a similar - albeit bizarre - motion of p

creatures.label: imperial toad
creatures.desc: The imperial toad is native to the cave systems below deserts on the Rim. It tends to be preyed upon quite easily but many cave dwellers have taken a shine to it as a pet due to its regal posture.

creatures.label: gorg
creatures.desc: Gorgs, known as 'chubas' in Huttese, were small precocious amphibians that could be found on several planets. They were popularly favored as food by many humanoid species. Thus they became popular livestock on sparse worlds due to their high temperature tolerance, minimal food consumption and fast breeding.

creatures.label: igitz
creatures.desc: Igitz were a species of small amphibians hailing from the planet Naboo. Those blue-skinned, omnivorous critters dwelled in the planet's many dense swamps. Because of the environment in which they had evolved, the igitz were well-adapted to both land and water: while their front paws were clawed for treading on land, their hindquarters were finned, allowing it speed when in water. The igitz were a

creatures.label: loth-cat
creatures.desc: Loth-cats were a non-sentient feline species from the planet Lothal. They were small, temperamental creatures, and while at times friendly, were still able hunters with sharp teeth and claws. They were often kept as pets.

creatures.label: frilled gorg
creatures.desc: Frilled Gorgs, were small frilled amphibians that could be found on several planets. This subspecies was notable for the frills along it's back and tail (hence the name) and for being slightly more aggressive in nature. Their spread to others worlds is often the consequence of culinary import of either eggs or escaped live specimens.

creatures.label: sketto
creatures.desc: Skettos were carnivorous flying reptiles that dwelled in the caverns of the planet Tatooine. Only emerging at daybreak and twilight, they possessed many rods in their eyes to assist their vision in low-light conditions as they ate airborne insects. Though reptilian, they were warm-blooded and gave birth to a single offspring at a time. Their small size and lower metabolism made them excellent stow

creatures.label: moss beetle
creatures.desc:
A large beetle, commonly found in dark, damp places.

It feeds off low underbrush in fungal forests and while not the best source of meat, it works when little else is available.

creatures.label: fungal ferret
creatures.desc: The fungus growing on the back of this small mammal has formed a mutual bond with its host, living primarily within and on its fur.

creatures.label: fungal weevil
creatures.desc: Unlike normal fungal infestations within insects, this infestation has somehow grown into a healthy symbiosis. The insect's movements help to spread the fungal spores while its body provides the fungus a home. In return, the fungus helps its host hide within the fungal growths of the biome.

creatures.label: Pufferpig
creatures.desc: Pufferpigs were a non-sentient, herbivorous porcine species native to the planet Kyryll. Puffer pigs were occasionally bred for their meat, which was consumable by several sentient species and resulted in the animal being exported to numerous planets. The true value of a Puffer pig was it's ability to sniff out certain precious metals.

creatures.label: longtail gorg
creatures.desc: Longtail Gorgs, were small tailed amphibians that could be found on several planets. This subspecies was slightly larger than the usual and had a tail (hence the name) and could lay unfertilized eggs. Their spread can be attributed to this variety being a favoured snack among the Hutt species.

creatures.label: terrorworm

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <HiveMind> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: An alien (or at least unknown) worm. It is large enough to pose a threat to a human, however they do not seem incredibly fast or ferocious They are often accompanied by other Horrors and seem to have a supporting role in the hive.

creatures.label: urusai
creatures.desc: Urusai were winged reptavians native to the desert planet Tatooine. They were predominantly opportunistic scavengers of carrion that would use the thermal currents of their homeworld to travel far and wide in search of an easy meal. Their tolerance to harsh climates and propensity to be clean, efficive corpse disposal meant they were spread to numerous worlds by various corporate and criminal orga

creatures.label: megavole
creatures.desc: A massive burrowing rodent, bred for its size and strength. It's almost completely blind but can be surprisingly aggressive when cornered. On some low-tech worlds, these creatures are trained to dig for valuable minerals.

creatures.label: massiff
creatures.desc: Massiffs were reptilian creatures found on both Geonosis and Tatooine, although it's planet of origin is unknown. Massiffs were reptiles that had coarse skin, large jaws, toothy mouths, big dark eyes and a line of hard spikes along their backs. Canine in appearance with an armored hide, the beasts could be domesticated and used for sentry and guard tasks and were often exported to other worlds for

creatures.label: truffle mole
creatures.desc: Thought to be related in some strange way to the truffle pigs of Earth, this mole has a specialized sense of smell, enabling it to find rare fungi.

creatures.label: wildpawn

creatures.desc: Wildpawns are a variant of the wildpods that have adapted to life outside of swamps and rainforests. Since they have less access to water and rotting vegetation, they grow much less, and are much less dangerous. Wildpawns are less resistant to gunfire, but retain the weakness to fire of their bigger brethren. Wildpawns reproduce asexually by releasing clumps of spores every few weeks, so its child

creatures.label: karabal

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
A large nocturnal bat-like creature who lives in the arid wastes of the world. They primarily feed on blood, which they suck off sleeping animals when twilight descends on the cold dunes.

While weaker and smaller than a wolf, the karabal makes up for its size with its bite, injecting an anti-coagulant venom that greatly increases the threat of blood loss.

creatures.label: eopie
creatures.desc: Eopies were a species of quadrupedal mammallian herbivores native to the planet Tatooine. These tough creatures were acclimated to their homeworld's endless deserts, and as a result were domesticated and exported offworld as pack animals. The eopie's rough skin helped to protect it against the heat while its hooves were adapted to climbing rocky cliffs.

creatures.desc:

A fairly new species of paravian theropod that shines a brilliant hue of rainbow colours. While not exactly strong, they are quite viscious and are not afraid to attack things bigger than itself.

creatures.label: Diplocaulus
creatures.desc:

A unique lepospondyl amphibian that lived during the late carboniferous period, related to modern day amphibians such as newts, frogs and caecilians. It has a bowed head that allow it to reduce water drag when striking prey from beneath the currents, a bizarre skeletal structure that is essentially exclusive t

creatures.label: Meganeura
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03827-1893 [MEGANEURA MONYI] CODENAME: NEURON >167

A large extinct species of dragonfly. Their wings are extremely detailed and are covered in a large network of veins spread across the translucent membrane. Quick and pretty.

creatures.label: Qantassaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #02012-1999 [QANTASSAURUS INTREPIDUS] CODENAME: DAUNTLESS >993

A small striped ornithischian. Obscure, but perhaps most well known for the mass stampede tracks created by this creature and Timimus hermani in the australian flats.

creatures.label: painted spat
creatures.desc: The painted spat was an avian predator believed to have originated on the planet Talus. A mutated variant (possibly from toxic exposure), this creature was larger, stronger and more resistant than other spat subspecies.

creatures.label: Jamel
creatures.desc: Jamel were a slow moving reptomammal creature native to the planet Utapau. Jamels were one of the many creatures used as beasts of burden on their planet of origin and exported offworld for such purposes. Their natural resilience meant they made great livestock even in harsh environments.

creatures.label: jerbal
creatures.desc: A large kangaroo-like gerbil adapted to desert environments. It uses its tail to store fat. It can go for long periods without eating when food is unavailable.

creatures.label: sand lion
creatures.desc: The Sand Lion is a variant of the genetically modified arctic lion, specifically engineered as ambush units by the navy for extreme high temperature environments. Instead of a light reflecting pelt, the sand lion has the unique ability of constantly digging into sand, producing dense clouds of particulate matter that obscures line of sight of its prey, making it easier for the lion to attack them.

creatures.label: Bagaceratops
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #389432-1975 [BAGACERATOPS ROZHDESTVENSKYI] CODENAME: SMALL-HORN >5222

A small, primitive ceratopsian that lived in harsh, arid environments. Despite appearing quite late in the mesozoic timeline, this dinosaur was primitive compared to relatives at the time. Its sharp, curved beak allowed it to shred through cyads, confiers and ferns. Bagaceratops would have travell

creatures.label: orray
creatures.desc: Orrays were leathery-skinned reptilian quadrupeds native to the planet Geonosis. The orray had great strength and a quick gait; making it a popular pack animal when domesticated (especially on arid worlds). The orrays used their long snouts to root for insects in time of food scarcity.

creatures.label: megatardi

evidence.why: bursts into a tox cloud when killed

creatures.desc: The Megatardi is a massive and curious creature, mutated from its tiny tardigrade origins to become a behemoth of the wasteland. Though slow and blind, it requires very little sustenance to survive and can consume even the most toxic wastepacks. With its six legs, the Megatardi is an impressive sight, and its gentle nature makes it a popular pack animal among those brave enough to venture into the

creatures.label: pilgrim
creatures.desc:
A large avian often seen striding amidst the dunes. The pilgrims were given their name after their long migration periods which can last months as they travel from one desert to the next.

Pilgrims are often domesticated by the southern tribes to serve as mounts and for their eggs which provides nutrition in the harsh desert conditions.

creatures.label: barbslinger

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)
Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
A large genetically-modified scorpion. No one really knows where they came from, but judging by its ability to rip apart living things within reach and shish kebab those outside of it, it’s a monster made for war.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

creatures.label: mawvorr
creatures.desc: Mawvorr (also known as'crysfangs'), were a vibrant mammalian species native to the planet Voss. These brightly coloured chitinous creatures were predatory in nature but could be the right skill forms bonds with skilled handlers. They became popular in the exotic pet trade due to their striking appearance, which ultimately resulted in their spread to other worlds.

creatures.label: brezak
creatures.desc: Brezaks (also known as "Zygerrian gliding lizards"), were large carnivorous reptavians from the planet Zygerria. Their flat tail served as a rudder, and when controlled by a skilled rider, they were quite agile while in flight. Due to their prevalence within Zyggerian culture, these creatures were transplanted and established themselves on other worlds.

creatures.label: dactillion
creatures.desc: The dactillions were a reptavian native to the sinkhole world of Utapau. Dactillions shared both avian and lizard traits, with long, thin wings and thick, scaled hides. A dactillion's pair of wings allowed it to ride the thermal updrafts in a Utapau sinkhole, and its prominent limbs allowed it to scale the rocky side. An avian cousin of the speedy varactyl, the dactillion served as a mounts.

creatures.label: lizardochs

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc:
The lizardochs is basically a reptilian bull, an hybrid between a lizard and the ancestor of domesticated cattle. The lizardochs needs little substenance to survive, at least for a creature of its size, and can be used as a pack animal, which makes it ideal to use in caravans through warm and dry lands such as deserts.

creatures.label: iridonian reek
creatures.desc: Reek could be found on the planets Iridonia, Kashyyyk, Ithor, Codian Moon, Tatooine and Saleucami (to name just a few). Various subspecies invariably sprung up as the base stock adapted to new environments. The Iridonian Reek was bred as a 'war mount' by the Iridonian Zabraks. Instead of giving them a meat diet, the Iridonian reeks were given a natural diet consisting of plant matter to keep them

creatures.label: Baseopsis
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #04831-1889 [BASEOPSIS SIBIRICA] CODENAME: ORIGAMI >4910

A humongous species of earwig with a pair of terrifying looking pincers. While generally docile and would prefer to flee at smaller sizes, the enlarge proportions of this invertebrate makes them more hardy and a dangerous foe to deal with. Their wings fold like paper, and shine in the light.

creatures.label: Hellboar
creatures.desc:
Hellboars are colossal omnivores drawn to blood, rot and abandoned flesh. They are not pure predators, but their constant hunger and brute strength make them willing to chase live prey when carrion and scraps grow scarce.

The greatest danger of a Hellboar is not only the impact of its charge, but its infectious bite. Its mouth carries enough filth, bacteria and rotting matter to turn a small woun

creatures.label: uvak
creatures.desc: Uvak were a large, membranous-winged reptavian species with sharp beaks. They were native to the planet of Kesh, where they were used by the indigenous Keshiri as pack animals and mounts. It's was believed that the deities known as the "Skyborn" may have transplanted these creatures to other worlds before disappearing into Keshiri mythology.

creatures.label: zeer
creatures.desc: The Zeer were a species of long-necked herbivorous animals of unknown planetary origin. They were sociable herd animals. Their exotic appearance made them popular in both galactic zoological exhibits and circuses, ultimately leading to their spread to multiple worlds in order to supply demand.

creatures.label: sivatherium
creatures.desc:
Sivatherium are imposing herbivores of Earth's ancient megafauna, colossi of muscle and bone marked by thick necks and branching horns like bony crowns. Roaming open plains and forest edges, they command respect even among large predators.

Although generally peaceful, threatened adults can become living walls of bone and muscle. Their carcasses yield large amounts of megabone, and their horns are

creatures.label: mudhorn
creatures.desc: Mudhorns were large horned creatures that originated from the planet Arvala-7. The eggs of mudhorns were considered a delicacy by Jawas. It was this reason that populations of these creatures were established on other worlds as a result of unscrupulous bartering deals.

creatures.label: aberrant fleshbeast
creatures.desc: Something went terribly wrong. This wretched creature is struggling to keep breathing. Whilst it doesn’t pose any threat and will slowly bleed to death, attacking it can trigger its self-defense instincts.

creatures.label: ronto
creatures.desc: Ronto were large, quadruped mammals that were commonly used as beasts of burden on Tatooine. They were known for their loyalty and strength, being able to carry heavy cargo. Their tolerance to heat and relatively low food consuption made them a popular export to arid worlds as beasts of burden.

creatures.label: luciferbug

evidence.why: produces <Luciferium> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
A small insectoid, genetically modified to produce small batches of Luciferium extract every few days.

creatures.label: fancy rat
creatures.desc: A lovable domesticated version of the common brown rat. Fancy rats come in a variety of colors and patterns.

creatures.label: sand leaper
creatures.desc: A desert rodent related to the common surface rat. While its main defense is mostly being small and quick, it has some natural chitinous armor as well.

creatures.label: chaos chicken
creatures.desc:
This bizarre purple chicken, presumably made by some mad Archotech, lays eggs which, when fertilized by an ordinary rooster, can hatch into seemingly any species of animal at complete random.

All attempts at removing its hat have resulted in the death of at least 20 humanoids.

creatures.label: mutagenic norphea
creatures.desc: This unique insectoid's body is so adapted to environmental toxins that it cannot survive without them. It periodically produces a liquid that can induce mutations in humans.

creatures.label: chem snail

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <BMT_HermaphroditicAnimal> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: Engineered much like the surface-dwelling Boomalope, this snail produces volatile chemicals within its shell. Even the strongest predators of the caverns have learned to avoid it, as the chemsnail explodes upon death. Its slime can be carefully harvested for chemfuel.

creatures.label: fission mouse, second generation
creatures.desc:
Even though this creature is usually called a mouse, it has more traits in common with the banner-tailed kangaroo rat, such as a jumping bipedal locomotion.

creatures.label: bearmole
creatures.desc:
Not many people get to see a naked bear, and fewer still want a repeat viewing. This oversized mole-rat inspires plenty of fear with its massive teeth, but gets a lot of love and affection from those wanting a large, hairless pet that gnaws on the furniture.

creatures.label: gornt
creatures.desc: The gornt was a domesticated, omnivorous creature native on the world of Hethar. A naturally bred gornt would grow to a meter or more long and was supported by four limbs, two small front legs and two large hind legs. creatures.label: chickenhorse
creatures.desc: An agile avian that most people expect to be more yellow in colour and go “wark” every now and then. A delightfully speedy mount that can pull off some impressive turns, this hybrid has been bred even further with other species to make for more colourful and genetically stable bird mounts. creatures.desc: The Agaripawn is a subspecies of the Wildpawn that has grown in the secluded environment of a Mycotic Jungle. Its body is covered by Agarilux mushrooms that seem to be in a state of symbiosis. Agaripawns are less resistant to gunfire than Agaripods, but retain the weakness to fire of their bigger brethren. Agaripawns reproduce asexually by releasing clumps of spores every few weeks, so their child

creatures.label: warg
creatures.desc:
Heavily-muscled wolf-like creatures with vicious unnatural claws and an absurdly powerful bite. They will only eat meat or corpses. If disturbed in the wild, they are very likely to attack.

Scientists say wargs are the descendants of weaponized military animals created for population suppression. The superstitious see them as the tools of an angry god.

creatures.label: mancat

evidence.why: humanoid hybrid — works like a colonist

creatures.desc:
A creature originally designed for other recreational purposes before that particular laboratory of degenerates got glassed from orbit, they make for an affectionate conversation partner. You know, probably, most likely, until their particular speech pattern grinds on your nerves like a cheese grater.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive feline genes. A surprisingly large yet timid predator that can

creatures.label: spliceling
creatures.desc:
A bent and malformed mutant, vaguely resembling what was once a human. Its gaunt face is a patchwork of assorted features shifting onto itself without purpose. It moves erratically, seemingly driven by sudden bursts of sharp pain and an urge for violence. Though its thin stretched skin looks decently fragile, its unpredictability makes it a dangerous foe.

It is unclear whether a broken human cons

creatures.label: hurseman

evidence.why: humanoid hybrid — works like a colonist

creatures.desc: An extremely cursed riding companion that can vocally explain in excruciating detail the troubles it goes through as a beast of burden. Most people don’t like to be reminded that animals are capable of feeling, especially if they can vocalise themselves in human speech. Don’t be surprised if no one wants to eat or wear butchered parts of this creature, as it looks like a misshapen human with clove

creatures.label: manffalo

evidence.why: humanoid hybrid — works like a colonist

creatures.desc:
Considered a straight upgrade from their progenitor, featured several times in Cannibal Monthly. Produces appreciable amounts of wool and milk, it is a living, breathing reference to the phrase “what does not kill me makes me stronger”. At least, when it comes to hauling large loads, which is all some people care about.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Capable of surviving very hig

creatures.label: bovine beetle
creatures.desc: A large beetle originally from Caveworlds, this bug is often kept in farms for its production of a milk-like substance and flakes of chitin.

creatures.label: groundffalo

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <GR_AnimalDiggerDraftable> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc:
The horned groundffalo is a great pack beast (albeit a bit slow) capable of producing milk and wool, as well as mining for your colony. Compared to a Groundrunner it won't be as efficient on its mining work, but the other characteristics make up for this.

Useful abilities: Produces wool, milk, acts as a pack beast and  mines rocks and minerals.

creatures.label: splicefiend
creatures.desc:
A towering mutant angered and prodded by its endless agony. Its proportions are wildly distorted, with its arms dragging along the floor. Its bursting chest is stretched open wide with straining cords of flesh, as it walks with legs thick enough to shatter stone underfoot.

Unlike its sluggish kin, the splicefiend moves with alarming speed and precision, overwhelming prey with violent charges and

creatures.label: Euoplocephalus
creatures.desc:

A powerful and tanky ankylosaurid that is more brawn than brain. Gentle and docile until angered, these dinosaurs pack a very painful punch when enraged.

creatures.label: drainer larva
creatures.desc: A mostly harmless, cat-sized lepidopteran with brightly coloured wings. Drainers were originally blue morpho butterflies that mutated due to exposure to high levels of radiation in some wretched planet of the Rim. Though they can feed on grass if there is no other food available, they are actually electrovores, feeding on any available source of electricity. Unfortunately for colonies on the Rim,

creatures.label: lemming
creatures.desc: A small rodent fond of colder climates. They're a tasty snack for most predators!

creatures.label: voorpak
creatures.desc: Voorpaks were a non-sentient but still quite smart species of puffy-looking mammalians that were native to the planet of Naboo. Diminutive carnivores, voorpaks were much beloved by many due to their cuteness and as pets which in turn led to their export to many other worlds.

creatures.label: raccoon
creatures.desc: A small, hardy animal that ranges wide across forests and shrubland. It is happy to break into your garbage container, or your kitchen, to eat almost anything.

creatures.label: turkey
creatures.desc: A short, fat, flightless bird known for its hilarious 'gobbling' call. It has been long domesticated, but also lives in the wild.

creatures.label: wolverine
creatures.desc: A small but ferocious predator. Wolverines are solitary animals that prefer to eat carrion but can kill animals many times their size if needed.

creatures.label: rabbuck
creatures.desc: Heavily built with rolls of insulating fat, the rabbuck is found in the far north of the continent, in the region of the tundra and coniferous forests.

creatures.label: dwarven muffton

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
The dwarven muffton is sheep-like herbivore known for its warm brown wool and gigantic horns. Herds can be often seen hopping around in the cold northern mountains where they live most of the year. Prideful and with a firey temperament, the males tends to fight by ramming their heads until one or the other is killed.

There are tales of a stoneborn king who fought countless battles on the back of

creatures.label: bordok
creatures.desc: The bordoks were a vaguely equine herbivore native to the forest moon of Endor. They were used on many worlds as pack animals when tamed. Bordoks were very sure-footed and, in spite of their size, capable of carrying large loads.

creatures.label: gigantelope
creatures.desc:
Gigantelopes were once designed as bigger, more powerful variants of the muffalo. An ideal pack beast that carries more weight than their body mass would usually allow. While they are mammals, Gigantelopes have pneumatized bones, meaning they have hollow spaces within them: pneumatized bones are strong, dense and sturdy without being heavy.

The gigantelope has a variable carrying capacity, set by

creatures.label: groundrunner

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <AA_AnimalDigger> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc:
A strange chimera between a bear and mole, Groundrunners originally came from Cave Worlds. They were used as walking heavy tools by the locals when they hit parts that plasteel can’t break, and for hauling large boulders that their owners can’t lift.

Due to their domesticated origins, they are surprisingly docile and easy to tame. Their incredible strength and sharp claws allows them to break roc

creatures.label: bearded troll
creatures.desc:
This large, eyeless predator roams the frigid landscape, constantly in search of food. During winter, they often retreat deep into underground burrows, to feast on the many corpses they hoarded throughout the rest of the year. Relentless and capable of quickly regenerating its wounds, it allows the trolls to take down creatures much stronger than itself.

Trolls spread quickly and are considered a

creatures.label: feral grazer
creatures.desc: These slow-moving herbivorous mammalia were native to Alderaan. 'Feral' or 'wild' grazers were significantly leaner than the fatter and more well-fed domestic grazer; however both species were distantly related to Nerfs. Their horns, tough leathery hides and fat layers acted as an additional defense against predation.

creatures.label: gigantelope
creatures.desc: An enormous creature with short legs. These giant herbivores have long abandoned the antelopes running gait and taken on a plodding existence.

creatures.label: maalraas
creatures.desc: Maalraas (or 'Nighthunters') were a non-sentient species of predatory quadrupeds of unknown planetary origin. Maalraas hunted in packs, primarily preying upon cannoks and other small creatures. It is believed they used "the force" to assist in camouflaging themselves from both predator and prey. For a time they had heightened popularity with several crime syndicates as attack beasts which resulted

creatures.label: tee muss
creatures.desc: Tee-muss were a species of domesticated farm animals native to the jungle planet Onderon. They were found on various worlds around the galaxy due to escape from domestic populations.

creatures.label: grizzly bear
creatures.desc:
A huge omnivorous mammal adapted for cold climates. Bears' thick blubber and fur keeps them warm in winter.

While their usual diet consists of fish, berries, honey, and scavenged meat, the grizzly is capable of using its massive strength and deadly claws to kill live prey. They are startlingly quick for such lumbering creatures.

creatures.label: jakobeast
creatures.desc: Jakobeasts were polar herd animals found in the tundras of icy planets in the Outer Rim. Jakobeasts were domesticated primarily for their meat, milk, and fur. While excellent livestock, they were ill-suited to serve as mounts, guards, or attack animals. . Jakobeasts were introduced by colonists that sought herd animals capable of defending themselves. As a result of the settlers' efforts, the crea

creatures.label: gualaar
creatures.desc: The Gualaar was an ungulate species indigenous to the mountains and hills of the planet Naboo. These creatures though tricky to domesticate had both the build and strength to make them perfect beasts of burden. The Royal House of Naboo kept a herd of Gualaar that were used to carry state officials. This regal affiliation and their physical practicality meant they were exported and ultimately sprea

creatures.label: raxshir
creatures.desc: Raxshir (also referred to as 'sabertooths') were a large predatory felines with bony cranial crests that were native to the pine forests of the planet Shili. It's striped fur help camouflage it when stalking prey and it was a natural predator to the agile kybuck. Their significance within Togrutan culture has resulted in the export of this creature to many of the worlds in which they themselves ha

creatures.desc: This lumbering mass of apparently decomposing plant matter is a Wildpod, a sentient mycoid creature native to some jungle infested planet on the Rim. The Wildpod is almost impervious to gunfire, with bullets simply being absorbed into its mass without doing much damage, but very weak to fire. Interestingly, it reproduces asexually by releasing clumps of spores every few weeks, so its children are

creatures.label: Nyctosaurus
creatures.desc:

A strange pterosaur with an even stranger crest. It is uncertain as to whether or not the crest had membrane between the branches.

creatures.label: worhin
creatures.desc:
Worhins are colossal beasts of the glacial plains, clad in golden-gray wool and carried by bodies heavy enough to cross snow, ice and open ground without hesitation. From a distance they seem like great herd herbivores; up close, they are living walls of muscle, wool and horn.

In the present, colonies that manage to domesticate them use Worhins as heavy pack animals and beasts of war. Their size,

creatures.label: megaloceros
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Despite being colloquially known as the 'Giant Elk', it's, in fact, not an elk but an enormous deer.
Megaloceros is an easily angered herbivore that can cause severe wounds with its extraordinarily large antlers, which are otherwise used exclusively for attracting females.

creatures.label: tetra slug

evidence.why: Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc: These massive slugs are a common sight among Glitterworld controlled territories, where they lumber about as glorified power plants. Outside of one, they are deployed as a mobile power source for Glitterworld research expeditions. It is rare to see one without the iconic power cores that protrude from their backs, as their unique bodily chemical composition is capable of outputting power that far

creatures.label: Quetzalcoatlus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #039920-1975 [QUETZALCOATLUS NORTHROPI] CODENAME: FIRE-BEAK >421

Perhaps the most famous azhdarchid due to its infamy as the largest flying reptile of all time, this magnificent creature lives up to its god-like name with speed, strength and ferocity. When left alone, however, it is truly a sight to behold. Tribals often refer to them as fire beaks, and ward them awa

creatures.label: Warbird
creatures.desc: The Warbird (or 'Sith warbird') was a species of huge flightless avian from the frigid planet Khar Delba. Sith warbirds were notorious for their bad temper and they typically used their large size to ram down their prey and gore them with their serrated beaks. After the end of the Great Sith War, Sith warbirds continued to be found throughout the galaxy, with survivors of the conflict breeding on

creatures.label: zygolophodon
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

One of the mastodons, and owner of some of the longest tusks in history.
While more primitive than mammoths, it's bigger, tougher, and more powerful than most of them. It is also heavier than some sauropod dinosaurs.

creatures.label: behemoth
creatures.desc: The Behemoths (or 'Sith war behemoths') were beasts of war used by the Sith that originated from the frozen planet Khar Dhelba. Wild war behemoths tended to travel in small groups of two to four and spent most of their existence searching for food. They were omnivorous in the sense that they ate anything they were able to find. The Behemoths were spread to various worlds with the Sith armies, eith

creatures.label: mastmot
creatures.desc: Mastmots (sometimes called 'motmots') were massive, thick-furred, quadrupedal ungulates. Being herd-dwelling herbivores, they lived on the harsh, frigid world of Toola. The indigenous Whiphid people hunted the mastmots, using the body parts for food, clothing, shelter, and tools. It is from this that the animal would often find itself exported to other worlds where Whipids would or did inhabit. Ho

creatures.label: horax
creatures.desc: Horaxes were colossal, slow reptiles native to the planet Nelvaan. They were capable of growing to huge sizes thanks to the low gravity of their homeworld. Their powerfully muscled frames were covered in thick, knobby, blue skin which provided excellent defence. The mouth of the horax contained many sharp teeth, the most prominent being the four enormous saber-like fangs that protruded from its ma

creatures.label: cougar
creatures.desc:
One of the most dangerous big cats, cougars are solitary hunters with long, sharp teeth and claws. They stalk prey from hidden positions before pouncing.

While humans are not their normal diet, they won't turn down a meal of vulnerable human meat.

creatures.label: beldon

creatures.desc: Beldons were a large cnidaria species native to the gas giant Bespin. They lived in the planet's lower atmosphere and could be found in large herds. They used the long tendrils on their bodies to gather atmospheric plankton and chemicals and so require very little direct nutrition. This variety appears to have been engineered to not only survive away from Bespin, but create useful Chemfuel and are

creatures.label: desert ave
creatures.desc:
The Desert Ave is a large flightless bird adapted to living in very arid terrains. Large bony plates cover its neck, giving it a much-needed defense both from predators and from the scalding heat of the desert sun. Compared to their more common Meadow Ave relatives, Desert Aves are less temperamental, but their slightly smaller size makes them less useful as pack animals.

Desert Aves are amazing

creatures.label: horse
creatures.desc:
A large hoofed mammal with a short coat, a long mane, and a long tail. Horses have been domesticated since ancient times.

When in a caravan, people can ride horses to increase the caravan's speed.

creatures.label: dewback
creatures.desc: Dewbacks are large, four-legged, omnivorous, cold-blooded reptiles native to the Dune Sea of Tatooine. As such, they are well-adapted to the harsh desert climate. This and the fact that they can be easily domesticated make them commonly employed as beasts of burden by both the inhabitants of the desert planet and the off-worlders wandering its dunes. Due to their numerous useful traits and versati

creatures.label: duck
creatures.desc: A very common type of farm bird, also appearing in the wild, the duck is raised for its delicious meat. It grows quick but lays eggs quite rarely.

creatures.label: tet'niss crab
creatures.desc: Tet'niss crabs were a species of large trash crab that lived on the planet Lanupa. Specialised glands on their shell would secrete a sticky substance which allowed the creature to attach pieces of scrap metal to their body for additional defense from predation. Sometimes this resulted in the creatures being mistaken for scrap and transported to other worlds for processing only for them wander off

creatures.label: frost ave
creatures.desc: The Frost Ave is a large flightless bird adapted to living in very cold terrains. A dense plumage covers all its body, keeping it warm and protected from intense winds. Compared to their more common Meadow Ave relatives, Frost Aves are ovoviviparous, a mode of reproduction in which embryos develop inside eggs that remain in the mother's body until they are ready to hatch. They are slightly larger

creatures.label: yak
creatures.desc: Yaks are robust cattle with a bulky frame, short but thick legs, and rounded cloven hooves that are splayed to help them walk in snow.

creatures.label: bursa
creatures.desc: Bursas were a species of ursidae creatures native to planet of Naboo. They had tusked snouts and feathery tufts of brown hair on their thick-skinned bodies. They were popular as circus animals due to their intelligence, but more often than not this resulted in them escaping and forming wild populations on various temperate worlds.

creatures.label: marsh haunt
creatures.desc: A marsh haunt was a 'Force-using' red-eyed creature that was native to the planet Abraxim, but they could be found on many worlds in the Mid and Outer Rim. The marsh haunt had dull, peeling, gray-green skin, camouflaging it in the swampy terrains in which it primarily lived. Its bipedal stance and skull set deeply between its shoulders gave its silhouette the appearance of a humanoid lacking a hea

creatures.label: megakrill
creatures.desc: While much larger than traditional krill, the megakrill is nearly as harmless. It eats algae and the like from polluted ponds and rivers. Some colonies keep swarms of them in ponds as emergency food.

creatures.label: arcturan sky eel

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
The Arcturan Sky Eel is a weird space-borne creature that inhabits the asteroids of a system's asteroid belt. They are usually not found on a planet's surface, unless they are somehow brought to it. The body of a sky eel is surprisingly light, and they have no problems flying through a terrestrial atmosphere. They also have electricity based defense mechanisms, and a faint regenerative ability.

creatures.desc:
Neutroamine is rather difficult to manufacture due to the sterile environment needed in creating a synthetic precursor chemical. So some insane madman decided to create a living creature that can synthesise its own neutroamine. Granted it’s not a lot, but have enough of these disturbingly powerful and quick cobras and no one will ever try to rob you, or live long enough to get away.

A reptile hyb

creatures.label: chickenlizard

creatures.desc:
Chickens are basically an evolution of dinosaurs, so someone decided to turn them back. Unfortunately they didn’t exactly bother to check that they should still be avian rather than reptilian, so it resulted in this nasty little thing that reproduces at an insane rate and empties your fridge. But hey, they’ll spit on your enemies and their right to shit everywhere, especially where they eat.

A re

creatures.label: reptile paragon

creatures.desc:
Small and venomous, with a deadly fart, not quite what one was expecting for the perfect reptilian form. I mean, you’d think you’d get a tyrannosaurus rex or something but no, it seems that the humble iguana is here to stay. If anything, the shock of something so small moving so fast has got to be worth something.

A perfect reptile animal, paragon of all similar animals with no needless junk gene

creatures.label: Aurora sylph

evidence.why: triggers a map incident by itself

creatures.desc: A wispy-looking creature that is the only known example of plasma-based life in the Rim: the Aurora Sylph is of artificial origins, and its biology is so strange that only the most advanced glitterworld technology could have been responsible for its creation. It is believed that the sylphs were created as a lifeform capable of surviving in the atmosphere of Red Dwarf stars, for utterly inscrutable

creatures.label: megalouse

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
A large genetically engineered pill-bug. These creatures once served as the frontline skirmishers of an insectoid hive; A collection of genetically modified insects made as a weapon against Mechanoid invasions. Their job consisted of reducing lone Mechanoid infantry to Swiss cheese; And they were good at it. Even the mighty Centipede was no match against the swarm of spikes.

Nowadays, they can be

creatures.label: freezer frog
creatures.desc: This small, herbivorous frog has special chemicals in its blood that allow it to survive in sub-zero temperatures. Due to the scarcity of liquid water, their young hatch into miniature adults rather than tadpoles.

creatures.label: darkbeast

evidence.why: Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
The darkbeast is a mechanoid-infused variant of the thunderbeast, in which the bioelectric organs have been removed and replaced with metallic spikes housing a distributed cloud of sun-blocking mechanites.

These deployable mechanite clouds can cover a huge region, blanketing it in darkness, and it is thought that the darkbeast was created as a terrorist weapon that attacks settlements by deprivin

creatures.label: windbeast

evidence.why: Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
The windbeast is a mechanoid-infused variant of the thunderbeast, in which the bioelectric organs have been removed and replaced with fleshy tentacles housing a distributed net of weather-affecting mechanites.

These deployable mechanite swarms have the ability to affect the weather in a localized manner, creating pressure gradients that may evolve into full-blown hurricane winds. This effect is u

creatures.label: slurrypede

evidence.why: produces <AA_DisgustingMealNutrientPaste> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
Although rare, mechanoids have been known to capture prisoners, and the Slurrypede is their solution to feed them in the most efficient way possible. The Slurrypede is a modified bio-mechanoid capable of devouring almost anything and processing it into a homogeneous organic slurry. This slurry is edible for carnivore and omnivore animals, but barely, and completely indigestible for herbivores.

Sl

creatures.label: muffalope

evidence.why: detonates in a big explosion when killed

creatures.desc:
A very naughty hybrid that can be told to relieve itself on command, creating puddles of chemfuel-infused urine around it. For those who just want to watch the world burn in the most vulgar way.

A muffalo hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. A bit too slow for a caravan companion but make up for it with intelligence and an unusual chemfuel ability that lends itself for defence.

<color=#E5E54C>

creatures.label: ravager

creatures.desc: This large, genetically-engineered insectoid is part of the Black Hive, an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. The Ravager was conceived as a space-bound bioweapon. Drop pods filled to the brim with Ravagers would be launched towards unsuspecting mechanoid ships, and the fearsome insectoids would rip through the ship's plating and lay waste to any mechanoid in

creatures.label: morrak
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Gomphotaria is equipped with not two, but four huge tusks that it uses to hammer and pierce its prey with.
Their seal-like bodies allow them to move very swiftly underwater but their huge mass as well as a lack of legs renders them somewhat sluggish on land.

creatures.label: thrumffalo
creatures.desc: One of the largest creatures in existence, dwarfing even the thrumbo and the mighty Gallatross. Capable of transporting a massive amount of material, producing a luxurious and excellent wool as well as thick, nutritious milk, they are almost the perfect farm animal. That is as long as you don’t look at your feed costs and die of a heart attack, but the scientists that designed this hybrid never ha

creatures.label: chickenlope

evidence.why: produces <Chemfuel> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
The ideal companion for those who love the smell of fried eggs and napalm in the morning. Regretfully they’re far too birdbrained to receive any direction, and most owners have been noted saying “I’ve made a huge mistake”.

An avian hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Very dangerous if allowed to breed uncontrollably, so consider liberal fireproofing and selling the excess. Produces chemfuel da

creatures.label: squirralope

creatures.desc:
It’s small, it’s cute, it’s a ticking time bomb waiting for some idiot to think it looks delicious. It’s not going to be a big explosion, but that doesn’t matter much when it’s in your mouth.

creatures.label: needlechicken
