creatures.desc:
This abomination is part chicken, part sentient cactus. If cactus nuggets weren't a thing, they are now. You can think of them as solar-powered egg layers.

Useful abilities: Needlechicken are decent egg layers. They can defend themselves with tiny poison barb attacks, and they almost don't need sustenance (except for a large amount of sunlight).

creatures.label: catalope
creatures.desc:
Have you ever wanted to have a cat that could start fires with hairballs? No? Too bad, this one does and if you’re unlucky it’ll be outside when it’s hunting. Which won’t be often, because those fuel sacs make for a surprisingly efficient energy reserve. Exploding kittens is no longer just a game, it’s a hazard warning.

A feline hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Intelligent, low maintenance

creatures.label: stoneback
creatures.desc:
These large reptile-like animals normally feed on the likes of cacti. If angered, however, their durable hide makes them quite difficult to kill.

Their longer back legs and strange appearance lends credence to the belief that they were engineered to live in arid environments. Why they live underground, however, is uncertain.

creatures.label: black scribe

evidence.why: produces <DA_RedTear> — not a normal animal product
custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
A shade amongst the scorching sands. The black scribe is a deadly insectoid capable of taking down creatures much larger than itself with its dreadful sting. The name of scribe comes from its feather-like stinger, composed of countless small quills that it uses to quickly inject a toxic venom, which greatly weakens its prey.

It’s venom can be safely extracted every few days, and while the toxin i

creatures.label: jellypot
creatures.desc: Named the jellypot for its ability to produce insect jelly in its large thoracic sac, this rare animal is almost exclusively found near insectoid hives. Despite being farmed much like ants do with aphids, it does not seem capable of breeding in captivity.

creatures.label: bogwing
creatures.desc: The bogwing is a fast flying reptavian native to Dagobah. They could be found on a number of worlds located across the galaxy. They mostly fed on small creatures dwelling in the lower levels of tree canopies (including rodents like leaftails) to avoid larger predators.

creatures.label: meganeura
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant arthropods, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The biggest flying insect to ever exist, meganeura, just like modern dragonflies, is a highly specialised predator.
Swift and agile, it used to have no aerial competition, which was one of the reasons why it had evolved to be so gigantic.

creatures.label: bumbledrone queen

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc: The Bumbledrone is a mutant wasp-like creature, probably the result of ancient genetic engineering long ago released into the wild. On its own, a Bumbledrone isn't very powerful, more a nuisance than a threat, but if threatened in big numbers their stingers carry a very powerful toxin that could down even the biggest foe. "Luckily", since they are not carnivorous, they use this as a deterrent, rat

creatures.label: splicetoot

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: A small, bloated mutant that crawls awkwardly on underdeveloped limbs, resembling a grotesque parody of a toddler. Its enlarged belly sloshes with rotstink gas, swelling and trembling with each jerking movement. Upon reaching its victim, the fragile body ruptures in a violent explosion, releasing a choking cloud of dangerous gas. Whether it was once a child or simply shaped to mock one is a cruelt

creatures.label: boomsquirrel
creatures.desc:
With adorable horns and long snoots, these squeaky lads are ideal in giving your enemy a stunning surprise. Their chemfuel mixture includes other gases that create a blinding and disorienting flashbang when remotely detonated. They’ll still make a regular boom if killed though.

A boomalope hybrid with recessive rodent genes. Quite fast and intelligent, these hybrids work as excellent swarm attack

creatures.label: toxalope

evidence.why: bursts into a tox cloud when killed

creatures.desc: A pollution-adapted cousin of the boomalope, the toxalope grows toxic pouches on its back. When it dies, the toxic material explodes and produces a deadly toxic cloud. Unlike the boomalope, the toxalope cannot be milked.

creatures.label: boombeetle
creatures.desc:
For lovers of xenomorphs everywhere, this bomb-ass bombadier is ready to launch sacs of acidic chemfuel at your enemies for fun and profit. Don’t expect a second pair of jaws though, that mouth is for spitting only.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Quite temperamental for a hybrid, but they prove to be worth it as they store caustic chemfuel in their sacs which can then be lobb

creatures.label: boomsnake

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc: What happens when you mix a spitting cobra, a rattlesnake and a creature designed to lactate refined fuel? This abomination, that’s what. Drive it into a corner and it’ll hurt itself to release deadly neurotoxins. Try and keep your distance and it’ll spit toxic blood right at you. Clearly someone was a sore loser in playing pretend games as a child, but had either the brains or the money to prove

creatures.label: manwolf

evidence.why: humanoid hybrid — works like a colonist

creatures.desc:
Possibly either the ancestor to the warg or an attempt at creating a successor, the team in charge of making this particular hybrid clearly had read one to many mythological novels. Arguably there’s no transformation at the full moon, so you just get the permanent single form, but there’s no pleasing some people.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive canine genes. A fast and dangerous hunter with almo

creatures.label: boomalope paragon

evidence.why: produces <VCHE_Deepchem> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
While more of a risk to keep around, they are considerably more efficient and don’t eat your crops as much. Plus their permanent sad expression just makes you want to pet them, how can you say no.

A perfect boomalope animal, paragon of all similar animals with no needless junk genetic data. Besides the various improvements to the baseline animal’s abilities, this paragon produces deepchem instead

creatures.label: boomffalo

evidence.why: produces <VCHE_Deepchem> — not a normal animal product
detonates in a big explosion when killed

creatures.desc:
People love efficiency and having one thing to cover all their needs. Well this isn’t it, but it gets damn close. The chemfuel sacs have mixed with milk-producing glands, which make for a milk that smells like pure gasoline and could almost power a vehicle.

A boomalope hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Has a large appetite due to it producing multiple products, namely deepchem, thin wool and a

creatures.label: cactus crab
creatures.desc: A smaller relative of the crystal crab, adapted to desert-like underground environments. They grow cacti on their shell for camoflauge and defense. From birth, they find a rock and settle into it as their shell.

creatures.label: boomabear

evidence.why: produces <VCHE_Deepchem> — not a normal animal product
detonates in a big explosion when killed

creatures.desc:
Originally intended as a way to make boomalopes more combat viable, their powerful muscles have instead been focused on compressing its produced chemfuel as a way to store greater amounts of chemfuel without care of how dangerous it is.

A boomalope hybrid with recessive ursine genes. Consumes more than twice as much compared to a boomalope but produces deepchem instead. They’re also capable of de

creatures.label: toraton
creatures.desc: Due to its sheer size, an adult toraton has no predators and no longer has any need for a shell. Small sections of the ancestoral shell do remain, however, forming an external support for the creature's muscles, which its feeble ribs and vertebrae alone cannot carry.

creatures.label: wraid
creatures.desc: Wraids were large reptilian creatures found on many desert planets across the galaxy (including but not limited to Tatooine, Ruhnuk, Korriban and even Tython). They were carnivorous creatures, relying on scavening and ambush to find their prey. Wraids were often over hunted for their valuable hides, causing their populations to spike and fall.

creatures.label: dinornis
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant birds, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The tallest birds to ever exist. They belong to the moa family and are characterised by quite dramatic sexual dimorphism, with the females being significantly larger than the males

creatures.label: flesh growth

evidence.why: grows flesh masses on the map

creatures.desc: Something went terribly wrong. A huge and weird growth has spawned within the electrowomb, breaking it completely and spreading all around. This growth is a hatchery for small flies that can devour any living creature to the bone. It seems to be sensitive to daylight, but no one knows how far it can spread at night.

creatures.label: mature fleshbeast

evidence.why: mod wrote custom C# pawn class
custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: The unwanted result of a genetic experiment gone wrong, fleshbeasts are usually miserable, weak creatures that ooze pus and struggle to keep breathing for longer than a few days. Sometimes, however, a fleshbeast manages to survive, and even thrive. Perhaps it was foolishly released into the wild, where it managed to stabilize and grow. Or perhaps it was stronger than average, and managed to subdue

creatures.label: polluwog

evidence.why: evolves into a different def at an age

creatures.desc: The larval form of the gastro toad. It lives in the disgusting waters of polluted biomes, feeding off any detritus and plants it can reach. It often lives in large groups.

creatures.label: batbird
creatures.desc: An engineered hybrid of mammal and avian, the batbird lives in shallow caves below the desert sands. It feeds on small prey and gives birth to live young.

creatures.label: fission mouse
creatures.desc:
Even though this creature is usually called a mouse, it has more traits in common with the banner-tailed kangaroo rat, such as a jumping bipedal locomotion.

The fission mouse is yet another example of human genetic engineering gone terribly wrong. Presumably, the objective was to make the mice more useful as laboratory animals by increasing their resistance and longevity. The unexpected result is

creatures.label: tainted turtle
creatures.desc: A mutated turtle that can withstand the noxious waters of polluted biomes. It cannot however survive its own toxin-filled sacs bursting due to high stress.

creatures.label: cave cricket
creatures.desc: While often considered a pest to cave-dwellers, some have domesticated these meaty crickets for their own use as disgusting but hearty food. They grow fast and lay a multitude of eggs in mere days.

creatures.label: plasmorph

evidence.why: Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc: This bizarre, mutant snail has a very strange way of defending itself against predators. Inside its armoured shell made of iron sulphide, specialized organs along the Plasmorph's body generate an electric discharge similar to those found in electric eels. This discharge is very low voltage, not powerful enough to damage most creatures. However, the Plasmorph uses it as a spark to ignite its own fl

creatures.label: manscarab

evidence.why: humanoid hybrid — works like a colonist

creatures.desc:
They say you can learn a lot by taking something apart and putting it back together again. Not this creature, it doesn’t give a damn, it just wants to take things apart because the hardest part is someone else’s problem. Some people actually prefer these chitinous creatures over actual humans as they’re not going to use up good material in a botched attempt.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive hum

creatures.label: mutating tumorfish
creatures.desc: The adult form of the tumorfish. Now adapted to an amphibious lifestyle, it can hunt in water as well as on land. Despite still being quite fishy, it can move with surprising dexterity out of water.

creatures.label: narkospider

evidence.why: can be drafted like a colonist

creatures.desc:
Narkospiders are massive subterranean spiders that hunt by ambush, preferring to sedate prey rather than overpower it through brute force. They wait in tunnels and dark spaces until a target comes close enough for a narcotic bite.

Their venom causes deep narkosis, reducing movement and perception until the victim can no longer respond. This makes the creature less explosive than other predators,

creatures.label: fungal mimic mantis
creatures.desc: A native to the fungal forest caverns, this mantis is larger than a person. It uses its fungus-covered carapace as camouflage while hunting. Unlike other mantises, they rely on their attacks injecting anesthetic and poisonous chemicals into prey.

creatures.label: energy spider
creatures.desc: Energy spiders (or "spice spiders") were horrifying arachnids that inhabited the Spice Mines of Kessel. The webs that these creatures spin between their legs can be harvested as Glitterstim (a potent drug and medicinal ingredient). This variety of Energy Spider appears to have been bioengineered to survive off of Kessel but with the downside that they have massive appetites. They can however survi

creatures.label: smoldersting scorpion

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: This colossal scorpion is found only in the deepdest depths of the earth. It uses its burning venom to cook its prey alive from the inside out.

creatures.label: maguana
creatures.desc: The patterning on the skin of this relative of the surface iguana resembles both cooled and hot magma, seemingly to blend in with the volatile environment within the cavern systems. They are naturally immune to fire due to the special composition of their flesh.

creatures.label: crystal crab
creatures.desc: A large and powerful relative of the decorator crab, cavern crystals grow from the minerals on this crab's rocky shell. Despite its strong exoskeleton, the crystal crab hauls around this heavy shell, the reason for which is unknown. They are not known to breed in captivity.

creatures.label: foundry beetle
creatures.desc: While herbivorous, this beetle is no easy prey. It uses its massive mandibles to crush both rival mates and anything that tries to hunt it. These beetles are often bred as war bugs by the more vicious cave dwellers.

creatures.label: royal rhino beetle
creatures.desc: A gigantic type of rare beetle that is revered by certain underground cultures for its rarity and power. While its royal purple chitin is beautiful, it is also extremely durable. The extremely sharp horn gracing their head fetches a high price. While normally gentle by nature, it is extremely dangerous when enraged.

creatures.label: pod worm
creatures.desc: Though large and intimidating, the appearance of this strange insectoid-like creature does not match with its otherwise passive nature. While it typically lives in insectoid hives as a part of the glow pod producing caste, it occasionally wanders off or gets captured and sold by humanoids.

creatures.label: tooke
creatures.desc: Tooke were small, hopping rodents native to the planet Naboo. They were nocturnal by nature and like all rodents, the tooke had a high reproductive rate and they generally fed on nuts and berries. They were a common pest animal that spread readily to many worlds including Stoga, where predators like the worrt would gorge themselves immobile consuming them. Even a carnivorous plant (the so-called t

creatures.label: needleroll

evidence.why: feeds on light instead of food
venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)
Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
Needlerolls are needleposts that have evolved to grow in the most arid and dry environments in the Rim.

Needleposts need almost no sustenance, absorbing all the energy they need from sunlight and minute amounts of water that they extract from morning dew. Like needleposts, they need a huge amount of sunlight (or equivalent). Nights won't affect them, but a solar eclipse could be fatal to them.

creatures.label: hermit crab
creatures.desc: A small crustacean found along coastlines. Hermit crabs scavenge various shells to protect themselves.

creatures.label: stone crab
creatures.desc: A robust crustacean with powerful claws. Stone crabs are a delicacy in some regions.

creatures.label: glowtail
creatures.desc: A small lizard adapted to toxic environments, it uses its glowing tail tip to lure in flying insects to eat. It's considered rather cute by denizens of polluted lands and is often kept as both pet and pest control, much like a cat.

creatures.label: megathrips

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: A large, genetically-engineered thrips. A worker caste of an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight against humans in large scale wars, it now often makes up for the majority of the kemian geneline hives. Megathrisp uses sharp mandibles to rip the armor into shreds, while overcharged acid glands coat the exposed flesh in corrosive substance, causing severe burns. A eusocial creature,

creatures.label: shyrack
creatures.desc: Shyracks were large, bat-like avian creatures with razor like teeth native to the caves of the planet Korriban. While ungainly and slow-moving without eyes, Shyracks were potentially dangerous pests, especially when they converged as a flock on an opponent. It's believed these creatures were spread to various planets as "live prey" for the others beasts in Sith armies (such as the Tuk'ata).

creatures.label: bloodrop moth

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc:
The adult form of this species. It flies near silently through cave systems in search of blood it can drain from prey using its razor sharp proboscis. Much like bats, they live in large groups.

Even a small group of them can drain a large animal to death in mere minutes.

creatures.label: macrofly
creatures.desc: A medium-sized bioengineered flying insectoid the size of a pig. The macrofly is the lowest caste of the Chelis hive, responsible for most of the resource gathering and work. It’s capable of lunging towards enemies at incredible speed, and it uses the digging claws to rip them in close quarters. It's dangerous in combat, but slow on open ground.

creatures.label: hellbeetle
creatures.desc: Not actually a beetle, the hellbeetle is a genetically-engineered giant insectoid the size of a bear. Designed for the forges of the planet Nuchadus, hellbeetles have brittle armor, but are capable of spitting liquid fire from their giant jaws. In close quarters, the sharp horns and ripper-blades will dispose of flesh and metal alike. It is, however, quite slow in open terrain.

creatures.label: fuelmite

evidence.why: produces <Chemfuel> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc: A large, genetically-engineered mite native to the planet Nuchadus, where it fuels gigantic megaforges of the corporations. Fuelmites are capable of synthesising volatile chemfuel in their fuel sacks, and can eject it from their fuelglands over huge distances. While fuel itself is not dangerous, a single spark is enough to set the area on fire. It is, however, quite slow in open terrain.

creatures.label: megawasp
creatures.desc: Not actually a wasp, the megawasp is a genetically-engineered giant flying insectoid the size of a cow. Designed as the hunter and the hive defender, megawasp soars through the air to engage enemies in close quarters, where it uses long and sharp ripper-blades and mandibles to cut anyone they face into pieces. The sharpness of the claws means that they are capable of eliminating even the most heav

creatures.label: acidspitter
creatures.desc: A giant, heavy insectoid with a large acid sack on the lower abdomen, that glides on a few tiny legs. While its armor is not thick, or its mandibles sharp, it is capable of utilizing its acid glands to spew gallons of corrosive acid forward. Due to being extremely slow, they are somewhat vulnerable to hit-and-run tactics.

creatures.label: dunealisk

evidence.why: produces <Synthread> — not a normal animal product
venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)
Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
Someone once thought that creating supersized spiders for synthread-web production was a good idea. Their home planet is now reduced to a Marble World; a world completely purged by atomic fire. The Dunealisk is a mutant variation of the Feralisk that has adapted to extremely hot climates.

Dunealisks attack by throwing spider webs at their prey. These huge webs stun and burn anyone they touch, all

creatures.label: gigalocust
creatures.desc: A genetically-engineered hunter drone the size of an elephant. It can fly over long distances, dropping down on unsuspecting targets, ripping them to shreds with its several sets of ripper-blades and sharp mandibles. It is, however, quite slow in open terrain.

creatures.label: lava flea
creatures.desc: Lava fleas were large arthropods native to the planet Mustafar. As larval crystalline worms, lava fleas were able to feed on rocks. The lava flea would then continue digesting rocks and other nutrients, shedding its protective shell with time. Lava fleas were also very suitable mounts and exported as such to worlds with inhospital climates to other creatures.

creatures.label: insectoid paragon
creatures.desc:
A terrifying callback to the original Sorne geneline, this mobile hive was originally designed to engage the mechanoid enemy head-on. By carrying an entire colony of insects with hardened mandibles, their ability to practically disassemble the mechanical menace proved just as effective at turning against their human overlords.

A perfect insectoid animal, paragon of all similar animals with no nee

creatures.label: doedicurus
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest known glyptodont. Its huge carapace is nearly unbreakable to any predator. 
Even though the tip of its tail is covered in spikes and would thus make for a decent weapon, it cannot use it effectively due to its very limited field of vision.

creatures.label: insectoid princess

evidence.why: produces <VFEI2_RoyalInsectJelly> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc: A giant, genetically-engineered insectoid responsible for creating new spawn. A broodmother to the insects in her hive, the princess doesn’t do heavy work, and tries to avoid combat if possible. As massive as an adult thrumbo, the princess instills fear in most opponents. Her thick chitinous armor makes her hard to kill, whilst long, deadly blades can tear through plasteel shielding in seconds. De

creatures.label: lylek

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc: The lylek was the most dangerous predator indigenous to the planet of Ryloth. It's strange biology made it one of the few creatures able to survive in the harsh heat of the Bright Lands. These dangerous creatures were popular exotic pets with certain criminal organisations and subsequently were transported to various worlds.

creatures.label: krayt dragon
creatures.desc: Krayt dragons are large, carnivorous reptiles from Tatooine, a desert planet in the galaxy's Outer Rim Territories. They come in two native subspecies and, despite their fierceness, are hunted for the valuable skulls.

creatures.label: war wyrm
creatures.desc: The war wyrm (or sometimes called the 'sith wyrm') were a truly colossal creature believed to have been created on the fourth moon of Yavin where one such creature lived in a large subterranean lair beneath a Massassi temple. The war wyrm was originally an infant exogorth that had been mutated and warped by Sith alchemy. They were very rare and very large and several specimens were believed to hav

creatures.label: kreetle
creatures.desc: Kreetle were a fast breeding arthropod native to the planet Tatooine. They were was often found in cities, homes, and other urban areas and were universally considered a pest. They gave birth to young in the form of maggot-like larvae. Kreetles thrived on dead creatures, garbage and vegetable remains (including waste). They were found on many worlds having stowed away in supplies and once escaping

creatures.label: hotfoot rat
creatures.desc: A genetically-modified variant of the kangaroo rat. They are capable of subsisting off of water created by their metabolism, allowing them to survive in even the most extreme of hot environments.

creatures.label: crescendo anole

evidence.why: mod wrote custom C# pawn class

creatures.desc: Most of the time, the Crescendo Anole is a harmless iguanian lizard that feeds on vegetation and small arthropods. They are unusually intelligent, and can be kept as pets. However, when the anole becomes aggressive in any way, usually in self defense, an unstable cocktail of growth hormones and biomechanical mechanites causes a runaway growth of the creature's cells, turning it into a hulking croc

creatures.label: hydra
creatures.desc: The Hydra is a fearsome creature, mutated by the toxic environment to become a three-headed snake. Living primarily in water, two of its heads remain submerged while only one absorbs oxygen. Quick and vicious in its attacks, the Hydra's bite is lethal, delivering a potent venom with each strike. Its ability to adapt to even the harshest of environments makes it a formidable predator, and one that

creatures.label: crested dragon
creatures.desc: Much like the prehistoric Parasaur, this lizard has a crest. The purpose is largely for display, but also allows them to make cute squeaky noises.

creatures.label: womp rat
creatures.desc: Womp rats were large, omnivorous rodents native to Tatooine that were widely considered to be pests. While womp rats were opportunists and fond of carrion, they were also predators. Although their normal prey included smaller animals, such as scurriers.

creatures.label: smog moth
creatures.desc: A large moth with wings with markings that glow faintly in the dark. This creature uses its bioluminescent abdomen to lure in prey.

creatures.label: mutating tumorfish fry

evidence.why: evolves into a different def at an age

creatures.desc: The second life stage of the tumorfish. It is now bigger and omnivorous, strong enough to hunt when necessary.

creatures.label: mucklurker catfish

evidence.why: swallows a pawn whole and digests it

creatures.desc: Huge yet slow, the mucklurker catfish waits along the filthy bottom of waterways for its prey to come to it, luring them in using the glowing tips of its whiskers.

creatures.label: lava snail
creatures.desc: A large slow-moving mollusk. Originating from the volcanic planet Nuchadus, lava snails were bred as farm animals. Their skin secretes a thick slime that protects them from extreme temperatures.

creatures.label: erin

evidence.why: Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
The Erin (Hyaena Erinae), also commonly known as a Corpsemouth, is a disgusting genetically modified hyena with reptilian characteristics. Erins were created as a perfect scavenger, greatly preferring to feed on already dead animals than hunting them, although if no corpses are present they will resort to hunting their own prey or consuming butchered meat.

.Erins will receive a considerable healt

creatures.label: junglelisk

evidence.why: produces <Synthread> — not a normal animal product
venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)
Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
The Junglelisk is a mutant variation of the Feralisk, adapted to living in the deepest, darkest jungles of the Rim. Some even say that the Junglelisk is the original breed of Lisks from which all the others originate. They certainly reproduce fast enough for this to be the case, and female junglelisks can be fertilized once and store the genetic material to lay eggs for quite a long time.

Junglel

creatures.label: Sporemole
creatures.desc:
Sporemoles are monstrous descendants of ancient burrowing moles, deformed by their parasitic relationship with the Mycorgloom fungus. Their bodies serve as living soil for glowing fungal growths, making them larger, tougher and far harder to kill than any ordinary subterranean animal.

Once insect-eaters, they became opportunistic carnivores. They ambush prey from tunnels, defend burrows brutally,

creatures.label: jewel beetle
creatures.desc: A small yet pretty beetle native to the desert shallows. Its brightly colored shell makes it valuable for its looks.

creatures.label: crocorse

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc: A rather muscular hybrid with an impressively long snout, this ravenous reptile combines adaptability with mobility. Unusually, its terrifyingly long maw filled with curved teeth is not used to tear flesh to eat but to imbue toxins and the required muscles to spray those toxins out. This means they have to eat a lot more due to their subpar digestive system and their favourite activities include l

creatures.label: muffalokomodo

evidence.why: produces <GR_PoisonAmpoule> — not a normal animal product
venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc:
Milking snakes for venom in order to create medicine is an extremely dangerous career. While this particular beast of burden proved to be capable in other areas, it was mainly synthesised in order to provide a safer way of sourcing an anaesthetic coagulant to be used in emergencies. Or someone was trying to get high by milking a reptilian space cow, who really knows.

A reptile hybrid with recessi

creatures.label: thrumbolizard

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc:
About as close as anyone has ever gotten in making a recreation of dragons from folklore. Capable of surviving in extreme cold or heat, the only thing really missing is a pair of wings and an innate desire to hoard piles of gold for a nest. That and the fact that it isn’t carnivorous, instead having an appetite for vegetables and wood fibres.

A colossal hybrid with recessive reptile genes. With a

creatures.label: dusk rat
creatures.desc:
A widely-hated rodent known for soiling kitchens and spreading disease, rats have a way of following humans everywhere they go. It eats almost anything and lives almost anywhere.

This rat seems to be markedly different from other rats. It is a purely nocturnal animal, and it has four glowing eyes.

creatures.label: murkling

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: A distant relative of the nightling, murklings are -in fact- quite their opposite. They are not as fierce nor are they proficient hunters, often scavenging in packs for scraps left behind by the more apt predators.  Their most distinctive features are the abnormally elongated structures on their snouts, which are theorized to produce specific vibrational sequences that allow for discrete communica

creatures.label: fungal husk

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
A bloated, shambling corpse animated by a genetically modified strain of caterpillar fungus, used as a biological weapon.

Fungal husks serve as ambulatory delivery systems for the fungus, attempting to reach and maul any living animals nearby to spread the fungal infection. This infection is extremely virulent, able to kill a human being in a few hours. However, it is very easy to treat, and it w

creatures.label: nightling

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)
Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
A sleek predatory beast with rows of quills on its back. The Nightling is a purely nocturnal hunter, hence its name, and isn't at all shy to prey on much larger animals, or people, than itself. Apart from its strong jaws, nightlings can throw the quills on their backs to overpower their prey.

Art by Gon (check more at https://twitter.com/GON_again).

creatures.label: muffalorat
creatures.desc:
Breeding a muffalo hybrid into such a small package means they have very little capacity for either wool or milk. They’re very quick though, and your handlers better be quicker on their daily milking and shearing.

A muffalo hybrid with recessive rodent genes. Very weak as a pack animal but they breed quickly and can be milked and sheared daily. The amount of product is small, but it’s thick wool

creatures.label: night ave

evidence.why: Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
A large flightless bird, black as night. It seems to share part of its phenotype with the Nightling, hinting that they both originate from the same planet: a RimWorld orbiting a very faint star -the native planet of an elusive race known as the Forsaken-. Night Aves have adapted to environments with very low sunlight, and they are purely nocturnal animals.

Night Aves are amazing mounts, much fast

creatures.label: dusk prowler
creatures.desc: A result of failed animal weaponization trials, the dusk prowler is an ideal killing machine, built and modified to satisfy the requirements of fast-paced warfare. The fierce nature of the prowler is reinforced further by the muscular protrusions on their back, which simultaneously act as both accelerators and as weapons. Their capability to overrun even the most well defended military facilities

creatures.label: muffalopede

evidence.why: produces <VFEI2_RoyalInsectJelly> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc: An oversized grub with udders that extrude jelly instead of milk, its hard-headedness serves it well in both getting what it wants and nutting anyone foolish enough to think they’re better than them. Allegedly there was a case where the owner was prevented from shearing the creature for so long that the overlapping plates completely prevented it from moving, who was afterwards thanked with a kick

creatures.label: snakecat

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc:
Possibly one of the weirdest and cutest snakes to be ever created. They have several tiny legs which are used to push its body along, while also having an invitingly soft fur. Quite a lot of people never stop freaking out from something sliding up the backs of their legs only to get softly headbutted by a purring python.

A reptile hybrid with recessive feline genes. An unusually furry snake that

creatures.label: barbed pangolin
creatures.desc: While passive in nature, this creature still has potent defenses. Its spiky plating has barbed edges, causing pain and bleeding to anything that tries to attack it and its tongue is covered with organic neurotoxins that cause rapid paralysis.

creatures.label: nightram
creatures.desc: The Nightram is a stubborn herbivore that shares much of its genome with the predatory Nightling, hinting at a common origin. They both originate from a RimWorld orbiting a very faint star -the native planet of an elusive race known as the Forsaken- so they have adapted to environments with low sunlight. When found on other worlds, the Nightram are exclusively nocturnal, instinctively avoiding nat

creatures.label: shadow charger
creatures.desc: A creature known for its mighty elongated horns, the Shadow Charger is actually rather passive, their horns only being used upon provocation or during mating. Their name is derived from their aggression against potential rivals during mating season, where the females are seen charging and locking horns with each other to secure a mate. While they were once used as battle mounts due to their speed

creatures.label: thunderox
creatures.desc: A creature often seen in the colder reaches of the Rim, the Thunderox is recognized by its shaggy thick fur and stumpy but effective horn. They get their name from their tendency to bray out during the dawn of thunderstorms, which is still used as a signal by farmers and drifters alike to seek refuge. They are reared in several farming colonies in the cold wastelands for their thick milk, comforta

creatures.label: nightmule
creatures.desc:
The Nightmule is a hardy pack beast, used for transporting loads or doing other heavy work. Nightmules originate from a RimWorld orbiting a very faint star -the native planet of an elusive race know as the Forsaken- so they have adapted to environments with low sunlight. They were domesticated by the Forsaken hundreds of years ago, and can be found roaming around some other planets in the Rim.

Ni

creatures.label: Crepuscular Beetle
creatures.desc:
A very large arthropod reminiscent of an oversized Hercules Beetle, the Crepuscular Beetle is a peaceful herbivore that originated from a mysterious Rimworld orbiting a very faint star, perpetually covered in darkness. This was the home planet of an elusive race known as the Forsaken, and Crepuscular Beetles were often used as domesticated beasts of burden.

Crepuscular Beetles are active during d

creatures.label: elasmobearium
creatures.desc:
The Elasmobearium is a hybrid of a bear and the ancient ancestor of the rhinoceros. The Elasmobearium is a pretty aggressive omnivore, using its horn to impale its victims and then mauling them with their vicious paws.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All primary bear hybrids have stun attacks. Aside from obviously being a very powerful creature, they produce a wool of excellent quality.

creatures.label: thrumbospider
creatures.desc:
A leftover bioweapon from a now extinct civilisation designed to completely eradicate biomes with dense vegetation. Records indicate that the local indigineous tribes were very resistant to corporate takeover and the megacorp in charge wanted to reduce profit losses. Eventually the planet starved as they were unable to stop these creatures from feasting on farmlands and food reserves.

A colossal

creatures.label: Plastemmoth alpha
creatures.recReason: tusks and shaggy coat, plus spines

evidence.why: can be drafted like a colonist

creatures.desc:
Plastemmoth Alphas are rare elder giants, larger and heavier than the rest of their species. They lead migrating herds through cold and temperate regions, carrying plastite plates so thick they seem fused into the skeleton itself.

Facing an Alpha means facing the living center of the migration. Its natural carapace blunts common weapons, while the amount of plastite inside its body makes it one o

creatures.label: summit crab
creatures.desc:
Legends tell of a great bouldermit that had grown so large and so powerful that it had entire mountains for a home.

This one probably isn't the sole originator of such tales, but it is a fine example of a creature whose path you certainly don't want to cross.

creatures.label: rabbitchicken

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
Legends say of an ancient and vicious monster, a creature so foul, so cruel that no man yet has fought with it and lived. This was a somewhat successful attempt, as its weakness lulls the enemy into a false sense of security so that it can rip their throat out. So do you feel lucky, punk?

A rodent hybrid with recessive avian genes. A tiny, weak, fast-moving pest with an insane appetite for its si

creatures.label: varmot
creatures.desc: A small herbivore that can often be found near human settlements in colder climates. For some reason, it tries to get towards human crops and stored food before any local plants.

creatures.label: butterfly
creatures.desc: Butterflies are beautiful, flying insects with large scaly wings. Butterflies are caterpillers which have completed metamorphasis.

creatures.label: black scarab

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: This large, genetically-engineered beetle is part of the Black Hive, an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. The Black Hive was designed to be much more aggressive than usual, and several new species were created and added to the Hive to increase its lethality. Black scarabs are little more than cannon fodder, released ahead of the main insectoid horde to draw

creatures.label: doedicoon
creatures.desc:
This armoured rodent is an hybrid of a raccoon and a Doedicurus. The Doedicoon breeds fast, and its armor can be useful in the frontlines.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> All rodent hybrids have fast gestation, as long as a fertility unblocker was used when creating them in the genomorpher. Armoured rodent

creatures.label: fleece spider

evidence.why: eats a thing nothing else eats

creatures.desc: Small and fluffy, these spiders have become a popular pet amongst the cavern-dwelling populace. It can be easily fed from whatever food falls onto the ground.

creatures.label: mossy fennec
creatures.desc: This fox species has formed a unique mutual bond with a type of symbiotic moss, providing the moss with motility and access to water and nutrients. In return, the moss provides energy via contact with the fox's skin.

creatures.label: unstable dryad

evidence.why: mod wrote custom C# pawn class
custom AI think tree <Dryad> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc:
A dangerous dryad caste that will explode with acid when dead. They can be commanded to explode... for the good of the tree.

In general, dryads are mammal-like creatures that have a symbiotic relationship with the Gauranlen tree. They reproduce together with their tree, which contains a hidden dryad queen. Dryads can morph into various specialized castes.

creatures.label: corruptor dryad

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <AM_Dryad_Corruptor> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc:
A dryad caste with the unique ability to produce corrupted Gauranlen pods and reproduce the Gauranlen tree along with its symbiote, the dryad queen. To do this, three corruptor dryads must slowly merge.

In general, dryads are mammal-like creatures that have a symbiotic relationship with the Gauranlen tree. They reproduce together with their tree, which contains a hidden dryad queen. Dryads can mo

creatures.label: ocular dryad

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <Dryad> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc:
A corrupted dryad afflicted by a bizarre extradimensional disease that causes gaping wounds to appear all over its body, from which ocular orbs slowly emerge. Ocular dryads can be further mutated into grotesque beasts by an Ocular Priest.

In general, dryads are mammal-like creatures that have a symbiotic relationship with the Gauranlen tree. They reproduce together with their tree, which contains

creatures.label: cave lemming
creatures.desc: This big, solitary herbivore can swiftly hop away from danger.

creatures.label: ocular nightling

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)
Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc: A mutated nightling, created by infusing an animal with the strange energies from an extra-dimensional corruption. Sturdier, more docile than normal Nightlings.

creatures.label: fenrid stoat
creatures.desc: A large species of mustelid that can survive both toxic habitats as well as fights with most other native predators. Its preferred prey is varmots and they are often tamed for the express purpose of keeping varmots out of farms and granaries. It is known for digging up previously buried varmot corpses, much to the surprise of new tamers.

creatures.label: bearffalo
creatures.desc:
A wonderful animal for those cold winter journeys, very popular as travellers snuggle into their fur at night to keep warm. Fights have even broken out over who gets to sleep with the oversized rug.

An ursine hybrid with recessive muffalo genes. Very filthy but a decently intelligent pack animal that produces good-quality wool and milk. Performs very well in cold environments and is more than cap

creatures.label: bear bug

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
This tardigrade-like creature is basically a huge bed bug infused with bear genes. It consumes a large amount of food, but its paralysing attacks combined with its resilience can be very useful in a combat situation.

Useful abilities: Bear bugs produce a powerful neurotoxin that can paralyse their prey, leaving them completely unable to defend themselves.

creatures.label: companion dryad

evidence.why: can be drafted like a colonist

creatures.desc:
A dryad caste specialized in general protection and utility for the gauranlenkins. Companion dryads are strong, fierce and loyal, and will accompany their mother wherever they are needed. They can clean, haul, fight and carry packs in caravans.

In general, dryads are mammal-like creatures that have a symbiotic relationship with the Gauranlen tree. They reproduce together with their tree, which co

creatures.label: elasmotherium
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest horned rhinoceros of all time. Elasmotherium uses its giant singular horn, placed on its forehead, to fight, attract mates, sweep snow, and dig in the ground in search of water and plant roots.

creatures.label: platybelodon
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Very unique kind of proboscideans, which, due to the shape of their two lower teeth is popularly known as "shovel tuskers".
It grasps tree branches with its trunk and rubs them against the lower teeth to cut them off. The "tusk shovel" is also used by platybelodons to strip bark from trees.

creatures.label: anima colossus

evidence.why: produces <WoodLog> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
The Anima Colossus is a variant of the Overgrown colossus native to the legendary anima forests.

It seems to be reptilian in nature, with cold blood, a slow metabolism, and a very weird body plan: it has six legs, two intertwined spines and six eyes. It has a symbiotic relationship with anima vegetation, with several Anima Trees and Mystic Cap mushrooms growing on its back. These plants seem to p

creatures.label: moribund gallatross

evidence.why: Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
Gallatross are deeply intelligent creatures, and they can somehow ascertain when they are close to death. They'll then instinctively direct themselves to an arid shrubland known as the Gallatross Graveyard, and die there alone, far from their group.

Of course, the timescales involved are impressive for humans, and a Gallatross might expend as long as two decades roaming around a Graveyard.

Conce

creatures.label: chickenrabbit
creatures.desc:
One of the few unusual animal hybrids that come with their own warning labels despite being almost entirely harmless. All it took was one absent-minded vegan to cause a single couple of “Breeders” to overpopulate and devastate the ecology of an entire continent. Fairy tales surrounding the fluffy terror have done nothing to help it be taken seriously.

An avian hybrid with recessive rodent genes.

creatures.label: pinkbird
creatures.desc: A small songbird with vibrant pink plumage.

creatures.label: Space Worm

evidence.why: mod wrote custom C# pawn class
custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: An extra-terrestrial parasite, the Space Worm has been given its nickname by Colonists across the Rimworlds for the way in which it slithers towards its prey. Once a parasite has successfully infected its prey, the prey (host) will undergo a series of symptoms from nausea to unconciousness. After 24 hours, infant Space Worms will hatch from the host, killing them in the process.

creatures.label: Colorful quail
creatures.desc: Small plump ground-dwelling birds with a distinctive plume.

creatures.label: manbear

evidence.why: humanoid hybrid — works like a colonist

creatures.desc:
What it lacks in ferocity, it makes up for in tenacity and formidable cuteness. What person, sane or insane, could reject the diplomatic arguments presented by a waist-high teddy bear with a face just begging to be pinched. Not that you actually would, as those sharp teeth remind one that it very likely prefers to debate with its food before eating it.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive ursine gene

creatures.label: mole
creatures.desc: The mole is usually found within shallower caverns, digging through terrain faster than it otherwise walks.

creatures.label: drainer

evidence.why: eats a substance no animal should
custom AI think tree <VEF_AnimalWeirdEater> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: A mostly harmless, cat-sized lepidopteran with brightly coloured wings. Drainers were originally blue morpho butterflies that mutated due to exposure to high levels of radiation in some wretched planet of the Rim. Though they can feed on grass if there is no other food available, they are actually electrovores, feeding on any available source of electricity. Unfortunately for colonies on the Rim,

creatures.label: green goo

evidence.why: Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
These amorphous, ambulatory masses of gelatinous fluid seem to be a mockery of life. Although they look like individuals, in reality they are part of a greater gelatinous superorganism, with only one objective: grow and expand.

They have been nicknamed green goo due to their ability to reproduce constantly, requiring very little sustenance, and quickly filling all available ecological niches. In

creatures.label: ironcasket beetle
creatures.desc:
A large beetle covered in iron-like carapace. Fearful and reclusive, these peculiar insectoids burrow into ore deposits to give birth, where their young can stay safe and absorb the minerals necessary for formation of their metallic shells.

Experienced quarry overseers often hire hunters to track ironcasket beetle nests, as their shells can be extracted for a hassle-free source of steel.

creatures.label: snoruuk
creatures.desc: Snoruuks were mobile mushrooms found on the planet Gamorr. They could be herded and were the favourite livestock of the Gamorreans, which resulted in their transplantation to other worlds.

creatures.label: decay drake

evidence.why: runs an effecter on nearby pawns
eats a substance no animal should
custom AI think tree <VEF_AnimalWeirdEater> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: Decay Drakes are large, winged flightless lizards that inhabit places with an abundance of vegetation. Decay Drakes release a nauseous cocktail of volatile pheromones that quickly accelerates the rotting process of plants, turning vegetation around them into mounds of fermented organic matter. They will consume these and usually get incredibly drunk in the process. Interestingly, the creature has

creatures.label: mime
creatures.desc:
Whereas most of the "alien" animals of the Rim are heavily genetically modified versions of Earth animals, the Mime is an absolute violation of all ethical principles: a ravenous, animalistic being created by genetically modifying humans.

Mimes are psionically gifted parasites, using their mental powers to disguise themselves as normal humans, infiltrating a human community and living among its m

creatures.label: worm
creatures.desc: A large worm. Its digestive system runs through the length of its body. Worms reproduce quickly.

creatures.label: Dilophosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #084729-1970 [DILOPHOSAURUS WETHERILLI] CODENAME: SPITTER >990

A small, crepuscular carnivore that is known for its large frill and the ability to spit toxic mucus.

creatures.label: Geralinura

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #034449-1911 [GERALINURA BRITANNICA] CODENAME: ACID >3246

A large, extinct species of vinegaroon. Their claws boast incredible strength, and, when threatened, they can unleash a large cloud of acidic spray from their long, antennae like tail. At smaller sizes, this merely stings, but the sheer size of these specimens can leave severe acid burns.

creatures.label: crystalback beetle
creatures.desc: A small and quick beetle adapted to the crystal-laden caverns. It secretes a sticky goo from its mouth to glue shards of crystal to its shell for defense and camouflage.

creatures.label: Pteranodon
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #0961-1876 [PTERANODON LONGICEPS] CODENAME: TOOTHLESS-WING >482

An extremely famous pterosaur. One of the largest known flying reptiles, this creature boasts an impressive crest and a powerful grip, able to lift a full grown man with ease.

creatures.label: harvester

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <HiveMind> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: A large carnivorous monster that attacks at night and attempts to drag off a living victim... One can only wonder what the motives of such a creature might be.

creatures.label: greatwolf
creatures.desc: A genetically engineered canine modeled on long-extinct dire wolves. These fearsome predators were created as pets for the glitterworld elite. Wild greatwolves now populate many planets, due to their tendency to escape confinement.

creatures.label: Wampa
creatures.desc: wampa were a carnivorous, white-furred species which dwelled on the snow-clad planet Hoth.

creatures.label: arctic fox
creatures.desc: A small predator adapted for cold climates. It usually hunts small game like mice and voles, sometimes burrowing through a meter of snow to reach its prey.

creatures.label: snow taraal
creatures.desc:
A cousin of the common taraal adapted to frozen climates. They wander in the frigid wastelands in search of carcasses from animals taken by the frost and snow hares for the majority of the year.

When the wind grows colder and the snow thickens, the snow taraals leave the northern ices to seek shelter in the mountains where they will hibernate.

creatures.label: northern drog
creatures.desc:
The colossal northern cousin of the wild boar. The drog is a gigantic dendrovore that roams the colder regions of the world where it can be seen tearing down trees to feed on with it's massive tusks. Territorial by nature, it will not hesitate to crush anything that earns its ire.

Despite its impressive size and strength, the drog is often hunted for it's thick fur and valuable tusks.

creatures.label: megasloth
creatures.desc: A giant, solitary herbivore with two giant claws for warding off threats. Long extinct after being wiped out by the natives of Earth's American continent, the megasloth was later brought back using advanced cloning and artificial gestators. Its thick hide is exceptionally strong and insulating, and makes a great leather for cold-weather clothing. It is peaceful if left alone, but will shred anyone

creatures.label: bullfrog
creatures.desc: A large frog known for its loud croak. Bullfrog legs are a delicacy on some planets.

creatures.label: poison mouse
creatures.desc: A smaller relative of the world-renowned rat, although this one looks a bit odd. They have a habit of making their way into homes and feeding on the contents of your pantry. It might be a good idea to keep a cat or two around...

creatures.label: dark vandal
creatures.desc: A creature of pure muscle, the Dark Vandal is known for its incredible strength. Often seen foraging in groups among the undergrowth, they have gathered renown for their fiercely protective behavior over other members of their brood. Once provoked, the resulting rampage is the last thing many colonies see before their destruction under the might of an enraged pack. Despite its infamous reputation,

creatures.label: agaripod

evidence.why: ignites violently / burns as a weapon
produces <AA_AgariluxRawFungus> — not a normal animal product
venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc: The Agaripod is a subspecies of the Wildpod that has grown in the secluded environment of a Mycotic Jungle. Its body is covered by Agarilux mushrooms that seem to be in a state of symbiosis. The Agaripod is almost impervious to gunfire, with bullets simply being absorbed into its mass without doing much damage, but very weak to fire. Interestingly, it reproduces asexually by releasing clumps of sp

creatures.label: taozin
creatures.desc: The Taozin (also known as a 'force dragon') was a giant predatory annelid with many arms and legs native to the jungle moon of Va'art. Finding their way all over the galaxy, Taozin were thought to be extinct but this may in fact be due to their highly elusive nature. They produce an rare curiosity from their skin when butchered known as a 'Taozin nodule'.

creatures.label: Empress butterfly larva
creatures.desc: The Empress Butterfly originates from an extremely rare type of planet – a Paradise Glitterworld. These planets have reached an extreme level of technology, but their inhabitants are very psychically sensitive, using their technology to offset any impact they might have on the planet's ecosystem and thereby anima. The Empress Butterfly was engineered as the perfect pollinator, gathering pollen fro

creatures.label: donkey
creatures.desc:
A small relative of the horse, domesticated in ancient times for farm work. Its goofy call is simultaneously annoying and endearing.

When in a caravan, people can ride donkeys to increase the caravan's speed.

creatures.label: bison
creatures.desc: A large plant eating mammal appearing in the savannah wilderness. Tamed are quite docile, but enraged are fast and dangerous.

creatures.label: muffalo
creatures.desc:
A large herding herbivore descended from buffalo and adapted for both cold and warm environments. While enraged muffalo are deadly, tamed muffalo are quite docile and can be used as pack animals.

Nobody is quite sure why they're blue - it might even be some early genetic modification test that just never got changed.

creatures.label: akk
creatures.desc: Akk (or sometimes called 'akk hounds'), were large reptomammals native to the planet Haruun Kal. Great companions, Akk matured from pups to hounds in a relatively short time and were often used for protection due to their likelihood to form strong bonds with their master. The illegal smuggling of these loyal but dangerous creatures has lead to them being found on many worlds.

creatures.label: reek
creatures.desc: Reeks are large, muscular quadrupeds native to the planet Ylesia. Their sprawling posture and immense weight make them relatively slow-moving. They sport two large cheek horns that can be used for head-locking in combat with another Reek as a show of dominance.

creatures.label: loth-wolf
creatures.desc: Loth-wolves were a predatory canidae species from the planet Lothal with a strong historical connection to the "light side of the force". Due to their intelligence and ability to co-ordinate as a pack there is specualtion as to how "sentient" these creatures truly are. They were believed extinct by most xenobiologists, so how they got here is a mystery.

creatures.label: drexl
creatures.desc: Drexls (also known as 'warbeasts') were reptavian winged creatures indigenous to Onderonian moon of Dxun. In early stages of Onderon history, drexls were feared predators that spread terror, attacking the primitive Onderonian villages. The creatures were later trained as mounts by the Onderonian outcasts, who came to be known as 'Beast Riders'. Their viciousness as 'warbeasts' resulted in them bei

creatures.label: Rancor
creatures.desc: Rancors were large carnivorous reptomammals native to the planet of Dathomir. Standing around five meters tall, with their long arms, immense jaws, and armored hides that could withstand blaster fire, they are formidable predators. A subspecies known as the jungle rancor populates the planets Felucia and Teth.

creatures.label: brown rat
creatures.desc: A widely-hated rodent known for soiling kitchens and spreading disease, rats have a way of following humans everywhere they go. It eats almost anything and lives almost anywhere.

creatures.label: timber wolf
creatures.desc: A rugged predator long feared by many ancient Earth cultures. As pack hunters, wolves have complex social lives and are fiercely intelligent.

creatures.label: infected aerofleet

evidence.why: produces <AA_BlueGel> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
A small, floating gelatinous creature. Propelled by the hydrogen it collects from water and various plant matter, these squishy creatures wander the lands, aimlessly bouncing off objects in their path.

This Aerofleet seems to have been affected by prolonged exposure to the gases emanating from an ocular forest, and red pustules and blisters are appearing in its exterior membrane. Its hydrogen see

creatures.label: glowslug

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <BMT_HermaphroditicAnimal> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: This bioluminescent slug is easily spotted in any dark environment, both by its own species and by predators. It is a wonder how they have survived this long, let alone to such a large size.

creatures.label: feralisk

evidence.why: produces <Synthread> — not a normal animal product
venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)
Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
Someone once thought that creating supersized spiders for synthread-web production was a good idea. Their home planet is now reduced to a Marble World; a world completely purged by atomic fire.

Feralisks attack by throwing spider webs at their prey. These huge webs stun anyone they touch, allowing the Feralisk to close in and finish the kill with their fearsome venom laced fangs.

Art by Feroxiio

creatures.label: rimclaw

evidence.why: bursts into a tox cloud when killed

creatures.desc: Rimclaws are giant apex predators mutated from iguana, well adapted to highly polluted environments. They are incredibly fast, powerful and intelligent.

creatures.label: basilisk
creatures.desc: With eyes that enrapture its prey should they gaze into them, the six-legged basilisk is both designed and named after its mythological predecessor.

creatures.label: crystalope
creatures.desc: Though weak and fragile, the crystalope was engineered to grow large crystals on its back. Other animals have learned to avoid it because of the huge explosion it produces upon death. Its crystal can be harvested.

creatures.label: nexu
creatures.desc: Nexu's are agile predators with four red eyes and sharp quills. They have infrared vision and are 4.51 meters long. Typically 0.94 meters tall, nexus possess sharp teeth and claws, as well as long tails. It's light build allows it to remain highly agile and difficult to hit.

creatures.label: acid slug

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <BMT_HermaphroditicAnimal> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: Originally designed for combat, the acid slug is one of the most dangerous predators in the earthen depths due to its highly acidic slime and flesh. The bodies of its prey are melted down to the bone within its gelatinous flesh.

creatures.label: crystalmit

evidence.why: produces <AA_RandomBricks> — not a normal animal product
eats a substance no animal should
custom AI think tree <VEF_AnimalWeirdEater> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc:
A Crystalmit is a Pebblemit that has been genetically modified to feed on minerals. Crystalmits have a partly silicon-based biology, so they can derive substenance from eating scattered rocks.

Crystalmits were created as a quick way of removing rock rubble from mining operations, but wild ones may prove to be a nuisance for colonies who'd rather use rocks for something useful.

Art by Feroxiious

creatures.label: pebblemit
creatures.recReason: rock plus red claws suggests hermit crab

evidence.why: produces <AA_RandomBricks> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
Pebblemits are bouldermits that have evolved in Rimworlds rich in narrow, labyrinthine caves, where massive size is more a hindrance than an advantage.

Instead of huge boulders, pebblemits use much smaller rocks as protection, slowly dragging them along the ground. Small blocks of stone periodically get loose from this rock, and they can be used as building materials.

creatures.label: crystal fairy mole
creatures.desc: Crystal plating covers the back of this mole species, offering protection from predators and hunters.

creatures.label: molebear
creatures.desc:
Far too independent to be a combat animal but certainly can both dish out and take pain. Works best in the background, minding its own business and digging up metals it finds. No one is really sure why but it probably has to do with those massive whiskers.

A rodent hybrid with recessive ursine genes. An independent predator with a very low metabolism and high toughness. Has an unusual behaviour w

creatures.label: bearalope
creatures.desc:
An unusual concoction of traits that was favoured by a particular client who was obsessed on making things explode. Earned the nickname Boom-Boom as they would often make requests along the lines of “two more booms, wasn’t paying attention”.

An ursine hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Lacking intelligence compared to a bear while also missing out on some strength and confidence in hunting. H

creatures.label: deermoss
creatures.desc:
Deermoss are large forest herbivores covered in dense fur and symbiotic moss. They move silently through old woodlands and, though generally peaceful, their heavy frames and imposing antlers make them dangerous when threatened.

Their coats host medicinal vegetal fibers that can be harvested by careful handlers. They also produce a green, bitter and nutritious milk, but raising Deermoss is expensi

creatures.label: engorged tentacular aberration
creatures.desc: A grotesque mass of writhing tentacles, mouths and eyes, quivering in violent spasms as it strives to breathe. This poor creature knows only pain and suffering, and will be glad to inflict it upon others. Created by infusing an animal with the strange energies from an extradimensional corruption.

creatures.label: arctic wolf
creatures.desc: An arctic variant of the old Earth wolf. As pack hunters, wolves have a complex social life and are fiercely intelligent.

creatures.label: polar bear
creatures.desc:
A great white bear adapted for frozen climates. Their thick blubber and fur keep them warm in winter.

While their usual diet consists of fish and scavenged meat, the polar bear can also use its massive strength and deadly claws to kill live prey. They are startlingly quick for such lumbering creatures.

creatures.label: megaroach

evidence.why: eats a thing nothing else eats

creatures.desc: This small, solitary roach can survive in nearly any polluted environment. While most roaches are considered pests, this species actually keeps colonies it lives in cleaner by chowing down on all kinds of filth.

creatures.label: granite slug
creatures.desc: The granite slug was a silica parasite native to the planet Coruscant. This small terrestrial mollusk has corrosive acidic green-gray slime blood. Its body consisted of four eyestalks, two retractable mouths, one foot, lung filaments, and suction pseudopods. One of their natural predators is the hawk-bat.

creatures.label: leaf-tail
creatures.desc: Leaf-tails were a small rodent species native to the planet Dagobah. A non-sentient species of winged rodent, leaf-tails had membranous leaf-like tails that aided in balance and camouflage.

creatures.label: neebray
creatures.desc: Neebray were flying, limbless creatures which varied greatly in size and habitat. They could be found on many worlds, such as Rugosa, Rishi moon, and Tatooine. There are several species of neebray, varying in size and appearance but all were tolerant to the vacuum of space.

creatures.label: waste rat
creatures.desc: A toxin-adapted variant of the common rat. Waste rats have evolved to be pollution-resistant, as well as larger, tougher, and more aggressive than standard rats. Their bite infects their attacker with toxic buildup.

creatures.label: pustule hornet

evidence.why: bursts into a tox cloud when killed

creatures.desc:
Predatory and dangerous, these hornets release toxic gas should they be harmed or killed. They defend their hives and their queen with considerable ferocity backed up by stings laced with potent neurotoxin.

They do not reproduce outside of their hives and give very little meat or chitin. This variety is loyal to the domesticated queen.

creatures.label: famine locust
creatures.desc: While small and weak, the famine locust can devastate colonies as easily as any raiders as they devour their way through fields of crops.

creatures.label: pustule hornet

evidence.why: bursts into a tox cloud when killed

creatures.desc:
Predatory and dangerous, these hornets release toxic gas should they be harmed or killed. They defend their hives and their queen with considerable ferocity backed up by stings laced with potent neurotoxin.

They do not reproduce outside of their hives and give very little meat or chitin.

creatures.label: pustule hornet

evidence.why: bursts into a tox cloud when killed

creatures.desc:
Predatory and dangerous, these wasps release toxic gas should they be killed. They defend their hives and their queen with considerable ferocity backed up by stings laced with potent neurotoxin.

They do not reproduce outside of their hives and give very little meat or chitin.

creatures.label: frostmite
creatures.desc:
A large parasite usually found in cold places. They sweep the cold barren lands in search of corpses buried in the snow, eating the preserved flesh and leaving a ravaged skeleton in its place; devoid of their former identity.

Art by Feroxiious (check her Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/feroxiious/).

creatures.label: mynock
creatures.desc: Mynocks were silicon-based parasitical organisms found across the galaxy. They were considered parasites by pilots and starport personnel. Their strange metabolism allowed them to digest various metals and components for nutritional value.

creatures.label: unshackled dryad
creatures.desc:
Dryads are small mammalian creatures that have a symbiotic relationship with the Gauranlen tree.

This particular dryad seems to be unshackled, and it will not leave the region if no Gauranlen trees are around.

creatures.label: krykna
creatures.desc: Krykna were predatory, non-sentient, spider-like creatures native to the planet Atollon. They were resistant to heat based damage and were highly tempramental, making them extremely difficult to tame.

creatures.label: ice crawler
creatures.desc: A medium-sized bioengineered insectoid adapted for extreme cold. In frigid temperatures, razor-sharp blades emerge from its limbs, turning it into a swift and deadly predator. However, when exposed to warmth, the blades retract, and the creature becomes sluggish, its movements slow and cumbersome. Highly dangerous in icy environments but far less threatening when overheated.

creatures.label: pustule queen

evidence.why: gathers other animals around a thing
bursts into a tox cloud when killed

creatures.desc: Unlike most other insect queens, this matriarch is very dangerous. She is nearly as fast as her spawn and packs a greater punch with her stings. Her stings inject a more potent version her species' neurotoxin, allowing for her swarm to quickly overpower anything living in their way.

creatures.label: pustule queen

evidence.why: gathers other animals around a thing
bursts into a tox cloud when killed

Her stings inject a more potent version her species' neurotoxin, allowing for her swarm to quickly overpower anything living in their way. The sheer bulk of her body prevents especially long active flights, forcing her to slow her movement for longer peri

creatures.label: snowstalker
creatures.desc:
One of the most dangerous big cats, snowstalker are solitary hunters with long, sharp teeth and claws. They stalk prey from hidden positions before pouncing.

While humans are not their normal diet, they won't turn down a meal of vulnerable human meat.

creatures.label: swarmcaller

evidence.why: eats a thing nothing else eats

creatures.desc: Found only in polluted areas, this insectoid feeds on otherwise inedible toxic waste. Unfortunately for any humanoids around it, eating said waste tends to lure in other insectoids.

creatures.label: megamidge
creatures.desc: Not actually a midge, the megamidge is a genetically-engineered giant insectoid adapted for extreme cold. In freezing temperatures, deadly cryogenic blades extend from its limbs, allowing it to deliver devastating slashes that inflict deep wounds and crippling crypto slowdown. However, when exposed to warmth, its blades retract, and it becomes sluggish and far less dangerous. Agile and lethal in t

creatures.label: frostling
creatures.desc: Perhaps a distant offshoot or an evolutionary relative of the sleek Nightling, the Frostling is a predator adapted to extremely low temperatures. The Frostling is a nocturnal animal that preys on the strange creatures inhabiting the frozen wastes.

creatures.label: arctic lion

evidence.why: can be drafted like a colonist

creatures.desc:
These large descendants of the now almost extinct lion were specifically engineered as ambush units by the navy for extreme low temp environments. Its fur is prized throughout the black market for its unique light reflecting ability and its tough leather provides surprisingly high thermal insulation.

Even though its danger and capabilities are common knowledge; many still attempt to bag its head.

creatures.label: blizzarisk

evidence.why: produces <Hyperweave> — not a normal animal product
venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)
