creatures.desc:
Someone once thought that creating supersized spiders for hyperweave-webs production was a good idea. Their home planet is now reduced to a Marble World; a world completely purged by atomic fire. The Blizzarisk is a mutant variation of the Feralisk that has adapted to extremely cold climates.

Blizzarisks attack by throwing spider webs at their prey. These huge webs both stun and freeze anyone the

creatures.label: Giant Cockroach
creatures.desc: An artificial insect from the old world, resembling a cockroach in appearance but reaching up to 2 meters in length as an adult. They are friendly companions in daily life. When trained, they can help human children avoid vehicles while commuting to school by flying at low altitudes. However, due to genetic modifications that removed combat-related genes, despite possessing mandibles capable of te

creatures.label: frostweaver
creatures.desc: Engineered for the freezing cold tunnels and caverns found in areas that never see a summer, the fuzz that grows on these beastly spiders forms into icy peaks. These spiders are antisocial and are known to attack when enraged.

creatures.label: thrumbungus
creatures.desc:
A gigantic, fungal amalgam creature. Rumor in the UnderRim says it was created from a mix of a failed genetics experiment and the fungi that feasted on its corpse.

While gentle by nature, it is dangerous when enraged. The strange hide that covers much of it is extremely beautiful and incredibly resistant to damage.

creatures.label: bobeene
creatures.recReason: bee body obvious, skull head alienates
creatures.desc:
The cheekily named bobeene is a huge insect created specifically to feed on the gigantic flowers of an utopìan Idyllic Meadow. Although based on an obviously insectoid geneline, they have been carefully designed to produce meat that is virtually indistinguishable from beef.

Bobeenes are peaceful, unintelligent beasts that are content with buzzing around the meadows, and make for excellent dairy c

creatures.label: goeto tadpole

evidence.why: evolves into a different def at an age

creatures.desc: The larval form of the goeto toad. It survives in the often murky waters in caverns, feeding off any biological detritus it can.

creatures.label: fleshling

evidence.why: dies unless its genetic timer is reset

creatures.desc: Something went terribly wrong. This wretched creature is struggling to keep breathing. Whilst it doesn’t pose any real threat and it seems quite friendly, it requires a tremendous amount of love and attention for it to find the strength to live another day.

creatures.label: brown bat
creatures.desc: It's a flappy herbivorous mammal. These bats flit around within the dark, using their sense of echolocation to locate prey, typically small insects or mammals.

creatures.label: bioluminescent bat
creatures.desc: Feasting on the bioluminescent plants and fungi within the caverns has caused this bat to adapt a similar trait.

creatures.label: gastro toad
creatures.desc: A funny looking toad bigger than some rabbits. It uses its sticky acidic tongue and wide maw to snag small prey. Some waster colonies tame and raise them for their meat as well as the drug-like bile they produce.

creatures.label: goeto toad
creatures.desc: The goeto toad is another attempt at creating a meat and egg source for mining exportation centers and underground colonies. The project rapidly got out of hand, and the specimens quickly adapted to the caves which became its new 'natural' habitat.

creatures.label: squall
creatures.desc: Squalls were small lagomorphs originally from the planet Chandrila. Squall instinctively seemed to want to be around other non-predatory creatures of any species, including sentient species. When in the company of other creatures, they typically begged for food or raided unguarded food stores. In the Core Worlds, squalls were renowned for their cuteness, and even further out, most beings found it

creatures.label: bloodletter petrel
creatures.desc: Uniquely adapted amongst the other wild creatures in polluted environments. Rather than feeding off potentially toxic flesh or plant matter, it instead prefers to feed off the blood of its prey.

creatures.label: spitter dryad

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <Dryad> — it does not behave like an animal
ranged verb on the animal itself: proj AM_PoisonBolt

creatures.desc:
A dryad caste specialized in venomous ranged attacks. Their ranged attacks can be commanded directly, or ordered to attack on their own by their trainer.

In general, dryads are mammal-like creatures that have a symbiotic relationship with the Gauranlen tree. They reproduce together with their tree, which contains a hidden dryad queen. Dryads can morph into various specialized castes.

creatures.label: tox-wool sheep
creatures.desc: Most sheep produce wool, but only this breed produces wool that absorbs toxins, allowing unmodified humans to survive for longer in polluted lands were they to wear clothes made from it.

creatures.label: spidercat
creatures.desc:
People really never understand what it is to have a bad hair day, and this feisty feline is gonna help teach them. As for those who don’t want to be covered in hairballs formed from silk strands and adhesive mucus, them’s the brakes, kid. Don’t wanna get spat on, then be friends with them and get over your arachnophobia.

An insectoid hybrid with recessive feline genes. Both quick and decent offen

creatures.label: wolfscarab
creatures.desc:
The answer to all your worries about escaping slaves. These omnivorous vicious beasties are effectively exotic hunting dogs, and the most exotic and forbidden prey of all is humans. That is, provided they’re practically unable to defend themselves. Everyone knows you can kill as many people as you like, just don’t hurt the poor puppy trying to tear your throat out.

An insectoid hybrid with recess

eats a substance no animal should
custom AI think tree <VEF_AnimalWeirdEater> — it does not behave like an animal
venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc: The Animalisk is a psionically gifted variation of the Feralisk, most likely artificially mutated, adapted to living in the very rare Anima forests. Animalisks are the only herbivorous species of Lisks, so they aren't as dangerous to colonies as the rest of their kin. They are however very fond of Anima grass and Anima trees, and as such can be quite obnoxious if they are not quickly controlled.

creatures.label: triple snapper
creatures.desc: With three heads comes the ability to attack fast and see in almost every direction. The triple snapper is an apex predator of polluted waters. It cannot, however, move very fast on land.

creatures.label: toxiguana

evidence.why: ranged verb on the animal itself: proj VAEWaste_AcidBolt

creatures.desc: The Toxiguana is a small, two-legged lizard that is well adapted to highly polluted environments. Standing about the size of a dog, this creature is not to be underestimated. It has a formidable defense mechanism, capable of spitting corrosive acid at any predator that threatens it. When it dies, a chemical reaction causes its body to rapidly decompose, releasing a toxic cloud of gas that can be d

creatures.label: chemfuel myrmidon

evidence.why: detonates in a big explosion when killed

creatures.desc: This ant-like creature was created as a replacement for the ubiquitous boomalope. Chemfuel Myrmidons consume both meat and vegetables and ferment them into a powerful chemfuel mixture, which can be periodically extracted from the animal. Contrary to the Boomalope, Myrmidons are quite resistant to damage, specially damage caused by high temperatures. They are perfectly content living in red-hot sem

creatures.label: giant slug

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <BMT_HermaphroditicAnimal> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: A huge slug, roughly the size of a pig. It is often used as a meat source for underground colonies.

creatures.label: metallovore

evidence.why: eats a substance no animal should
custom AI think tree <VEF_AnimalWeirdEater> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: Metallovores are repulsive creatures genetically modified to fill a very specific niche: eating metals. The writhing tentacles in the animal's mouth secrete an organic substance that is capable of quickly rusting and dissolving most common metals, turning them into small flakes that serve as sustenance for the metallovore. They prefer small chunks of metal, since they can be more easily digested,

creatures.label: crystal mimic mantis
creatures.desc: A native to the crystal caverns, this mantis is nearly the size of a person. It uses its crystal-like carapace as camouflage while hunting prey.

creatures.label: megapleura
creatures.desc: A relative of the trilobite beetle, the megapleura has grown to massive proportions while living deep within the Rim's crust. While odd in appearance, it is largely harmless.

creatures.label: cinderlisk

evidence.why: produces <AA_CinderSilk> — not a normal animal product
custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
Probably the most dangerous of the Feralisk variants, the Cinderlisk is a huge spider adapted to living close to the calderas of dormant volcanoes. Originally created to be exploited for their durable and heat-resistant silk, but once they escaped into the wild they began multiplying uncontrollably.

Cinderlisks attack by throwing spider webs at their prey. These huge webs stun and burn anyone the

creatures.label: mammoth worm

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
An extremely large, genetically-engineered worm. Despite its incredibly intimidating size and arsenal, these huge creatures are rather quite peaceful. It was once part of the worker caste of an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. It carried and moved things that its little cousins cannot.

While generally peaceful, if provoked, it becomes a terrifying force th

creatures.label: pillbug

evidence.why: eats a thing nothing else eats

creatures.desc: The large isopod inhabits the bottom of the cavern food chain. It feeds on virtually any filth it finds, keeping the tunnels and catacombs clean.

creatures.label: metallosnail

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <BMT_HermaphroditicAnimal> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: Adapted or engineered to survive the considerable heat and volatility near the molten layer, the metallosnail has gained the ability to grow metal for its shell. It also produces thin plates of metal to protect its softer bits.

creatures.label: black spelopede

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch
Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc: A medium-sized bioengineered insectoid the size of a sheep that is part of the Black Hive, an artificial ecosystem of insectoids designed to fight mechanoid invasions. The Black Hive was designed to be much more aggressive than usual, and several new species were created and added to the Hive to increase its lethality. The spelopede is the middle caste of a hive, taking care of most work tasks as

creatures.label: woolly bat
creatures.desc: These large bats have been farmed for their wool-like fur for generations. They were selectively bred to be flightless to make wool gathering easier. Their livable temperature range is shockingly wide.

creatures.label: acanthamoeba gigantea, huge
creatures.recReason: reads as a cell, alien at colony scale

evidence.why: eats a substance no animal should
custom AI think tree <VEF_AnimalWeirdEater> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc:
Literally the "giant spiked amoeba", this strange creature is a huge unicellular organism genetically modified to serve as a biological cleaning machine. Acanthamoebas will happily feed on most types of non-metallic trash, engorging themselves in the process.

After a certain amount of feedings, Acanthamoebas will increase in size and, after reaching a threshold, they will split into two different

creatures.label: sand prowler
creatures.desc:
A genetic amalgamation possessing features of a lion, a shark and a sand skink, the Sand Prowler was originally created as a ferocious hunting animal for desert planets.

.The Sand Prowler can quickly burrow and "swim" through sand, hiding the bulk of its body and allowing it to strike its prey from relative safety. It is only able to burrow under loose sand, with other soils being too dense to tr

creatures.label: bunker bug
creatures.desc: Whether it is engineered or mutated from a wild animal is unknown, but this massive insect-like creature can use its powerful claws to rend its way through steel almost as easily as flesh and bone. It does not breed in captivity.

creatures.label: hungering hydra
creatures.desc: With three heads and just as many stomachs, this massive ravenous beast almost constantly scours cave systems for food. They are protected by strong natural armor and their razor sharp teeth, with any injuries they do sustain healing rapidly.

creatures.label: greater krayt dragon
creatures.desc: The greater krayt dragon was the largest species of krayt dragon, and the apex predator of the planet Tatooine. Using its ten strong legs, it literally swam through the shifting sands. This larger subspecies is both rarer and yet it was still hunted (some say foolishly as most hunts end in disaster) for the precious pearls found in their bodies and as a right of passage for certain Tusken tribes.

creatures.label: black swarmlings
creatures.desc: The juvenile form of Black Hive insectoids, black swarmlings are more or less harmless, slow and easy to kill. After some time has passed, they undergo a metamorphosis, forming a cocoon from which an adult Black Hive insectoid will emerge. There is no way to tell what kind of insect will crawl out of its cocoon.

creatures.label: swarmling

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: Human space colonization slowly disseminated the Old Earth genelines across the stars, with all kinds of terran animals being used to populate and terraform the strange new worlds. Some of these animals, however, were pests, hitching a ride inside spaceships and multiplying at the expense of humanity. Swarmlings were one of such pests. Historians of the Ordo Historia theorize that Swarmlings were

creatures.label: Colorful stone crab
creatures.desc: A robust crustacean with powerful claws. Stone crabs are a delicacy in some regions.

creatures.label: gembug

evidence.why: eats a thing nothing else eats

creatures.desc: Commonly found in crystal caverns, the gembug is a smaller relative of the pillbug known for its gem-like exoskeleton.

creatures.label: anooba
creatures.desc: Anoobas were aggressive pack predators that lived throughout the Outer Rim Territories. Opportunistic hunters as well as scavengers, these wolflike canines would attack virtually anything smaller than themselves (such as scurriers).

creatures.label: aaroxis dendoria
creatures.desc: Uniquely engineered for life in an underground environment, this moth has been altered to produce silk even in adulthood, at the cost of remaining wingless.

creatures.label: raptor shrimp

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
A large genetically modified creature, its origins unknown. They are known to make homes in tropical regions, instilling fear among the local inhabitants as those who pass through its territory are often reported to go missing; their bodies never found.

The few that survived an encounter with these monsters report bullets being shrugged off, limbs of their companions being torn apart, and the sta

creatures.label: thermadon

evidence.why: Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc: The Thermadon is a large Blackspider that has been biologically augmented with volatile chemical glands. Originally, the Thermadon was bred by the long forgotten creators of the Black Hive as a fearsome fire-breathing shock trooper, using thermal grenades capable of affecting even fire-resistant Mechanoids, the primary objective of the Black Hive. Mechanoids however managed to adapt to these biolo

creatures.label: Protosolpuga
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03459-1913[PROTOSOLPUGA CARBONARIA] CODENAME: SUN-SPIDER >3246

An extinct genus of solifugae. They do not possess any venom or stinger, but utilise a powerful, pure-strength bite instead.

creatures.label: mantrap

evidence.why: feeds on light instead of food
custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch
Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc: Project Apricus was a classified scientific endeavour on one of the RimWorlds aiming to discover new ways to fight the Mechanoid menace using nature. The mantrap was created as an attempt to weaponize a mutated Dionaea muscipula (Venus flytrap) by implanting concentrated formic acid spit launchers on its jaws. This strong acid was theoretically powerful enough to corrode the plasteel on Mechanoid

creatures.label: Gorgonops
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #04355-1912 [GORGONOPS WHAITSI] CODENAME: MEDUSA >428

A large carnivorous therapsid with a mottled hide of tan, crimson and black. These huge creatures are often seen tailgating caravans in the blistering heat, waiting for some unfortunate soul to fall behind. Their codename derives from the stunning shimmer of their eyes, often described as a nebula of gold, said to

creatures.label: Molebear
creatures.desc: Created from a genetic mix of mole and bear, it was released into the wild and has found a home within caverns near the surface. It comes and goes as it pleases.

creatures.label: lockjaw

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
A very large animal native to this planet’s tropical regions. Nicknamed Lockjaws both for their incredibly strong bite force and for the disease they transmit, which afflicts its victims with a moderate facial paralysis that makes eating extremely uncomfortable.

Despite having a guillotine for a mouth, the Lockjaw does not seem to be an overly aggressive creature; Preferring to prey on the local

creatures.label: ocular slinger

evidence.why: can be drafted like a colonist
custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: A large, mutated scorpion. A multitude of twitching eyes look around nervously.

creatures.label: helixien

evidence.why: gives colonists thoughts just by being near

creatures.desc: The Helixien Slug is a genetically modified strain of the Leopard Slug, intended as a fast corpse disposal aid. Aside from the obvious size alteration, the Helixien constantly secretes a foul-smelling, corrosive gas that produces an uncomfortable, itchy sensation in living beings. This gas is mostly harmless, unless it comes into contact with decaying organic matter: it greatly accelerates corpse

creatures.label: black insectoid queen

evidence.why: produces <AA_BlackInsectJelly> — not a normal animal product
custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: A giant, genetically-engineered insectoid responsible for creating new Black Hive spawn. A mother to the insects in her hive, a black queen doesn’t do heavy work, and tries to avoid combat if possible. As massive as an adult thrumbo, the queen instils fear in most opponents. Her thick chitinous armour makes her hard to kill, whilst long, deadly blades can tear through plasteel shielding in seconds

creatures.label: silver sheep
creatures.desc: Silver sheep are known for the warmth and luster of their wool, allowing many a colonist to survive inside hollow glaciers.

creatures.label: feral nerf
creatures.desc: Nerfs were a species of antlered, herbivorous mammalia found all across the galaxy. Because of the nerf's ability to easily adapt to harsh environments, several defined sub-species existed and were often referred to as 'feral' or 'wild' variants of the same animal.

creatures.label: strill
creatures.desc: Strills were a species of highly intelligent, six-legged carnivorous mammals native to the planet Mandalore. They had folds of leathery skin between their legs which allowed them to glide short distances with sufficient updraft and they purportedly had a very distinct (often unpleasant) smell. A number of Mandalorians took to keeping strills (or 'striile' in Mando'a) as pets, making use of their n

creatures.label: thrumborat
creatures.desc:
Practically an overgrown and intelligent pest capable of tunnelling underground, so not even a nuke could clear an infestation. And it truly would be an infestation, as it has a gestation period measured in days rather than weeks, with a single breeding pair capable of wiping out an entire agricultural planet.

A colossal hybrid with recessive rodent genes. Incredibly durable and fast breeding, th

creatures.label: bearded yak
creatures.desc: A large member of the yak family, well-adapted to life in climates of bitter cold. Unfortunately for some, they cannot be sheared for their fur.

creatures.label: muffalo paragon
creatures.desc:
A return to simpler times, when everyone could have sworn blind that muffalos used to be able to produce milk but were instead fooled by hornless paragons.

A perfect muffalo animal, paragon of all similar animals with no needless junk genetic data. Besides the various improvements to the baseline animal’s abilities, this paragon also produces milk and can be slaughtered for a valuable pelt, which

creatures.label: grazer
creatures.desc: A large, slow domesticated mammalia from Alderaan that has been selectively bred to produce huge amounts of milk. Their fat reserves function to insulate them well against a broad range of temperature. However, most of them are so adapted to farm life that they cannot survive in the wild like their feral brethren.

creatures.label: thrumbochicken
creatures.desc:
This is probably the closest chickens will be able to get to recovering their past glory as super predators. They’ll often hunt any other animal for their next meal, multiple times a day, and you haven’t yet lived until you’ve ridden one on a long journey. If they could be further bred to cross mountains and oceans, they’d be almost perfect.

A colossal hybrid with recessive avian genes. The combi

creatures.label: thrumbalope

evidence.why: produces <Chemfuel> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
Now here’s a creature you absolutely want to keep properly fed, and you’re going to need entire fields to support a single one. The ridiculous amount of chemfuel they produce means that the ceasing of their life functions is more accurately described as “thermonuclear”. So if they are going to blow up, send them as a surprise gift to friends and family who keep trying to kill you.

A colossal hybr

creatures.label: hive queen
creatures.desc: The birth mother of an insect megahive. Under suitable conditions, several distinct insect hives will merge together and produce a hive queen. The queen quickly grows in size, becoming trapped in her own burrow.

creatures.label: gallatross

evidence.why: Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
Throughout every world,
      Flow the tale of old,
      A creature with untold might
      And an immeasurable height.
      Strength that machines can’t copy
      Power that so-called gods call heresy.
      Beware, beware would-be foes
      Beware, the wrath of the Gallatross.

Concept and art by A_Friend (aka SentientLine), the original Alpha Animals artist.

creatures.label: mycoid colossus

evidence.why: produces <AA_AgariluxRawFungus> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
The Mycoid Colossus is a variant of the Overgrown colossus native to a mycotic jungle.

It seems to be reptilian in nature, with cold blood, a slow metabolism, and a very weird body plan: it has six legs, two intertwined spines and six eyes. It has a symbiotic relationship with fungi, with several mutant Agarilux mushrooms growing on its back. These fungi trap insects and seem to provide sustenanc

creatures.label: boomrat
creatures.desc: Either by deliberate genetic weaponization, or as an unusual defense mechanism, these rodent-like creatures create a powerful fire-starting explosion when killed.

creatures.label: rikknit
creatures.desc: The rikknit were an arboreal crustacean native to the planet New Plympto. Female rikknit had ovum sacs connected to their abdomens, which when removed via butchery were considered a delicacy. Harvested ovum sacs could also be processed into an addictive substance called ji rikknit. It is likely these creatures are escaped livestock that have since gone on to establish wild populations.

creatures.label: ocular jelly

evidence.why: Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
The Rim is filled with creatures that might be the product of either accelerated evolution from terrestrial origins, or, more often, of ancient human genetic engineering gone awry. The ocular jelly, however, is so fundamentally weird that some scientists have speculated about a possible extradimensional origin. Or perhaps it is just some cruel, if elaborate, practical joke.

It seems to have some

creatures.label: red goo

evidence.why: Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
This blob of bubbling organic matter seems to be an extension of the terrain itself, a disfigured excrescence given a semblance of life.

The red goo seem to thrive in the strangely bizarre environment of the ocular forest, nibbling on the aberrant vegetation and periodically cloning themselves. NOTE: due to gameplay constraints, red goo will only self-replicate until the map holds 15 creatures, b

creatures.label: manalope

evidence.why: humanoid hybrid — works like a colonist

creatures.desc:
A floating, ticking time bomb that produces extremely reactive chemicals instead of chemfuel. Arguably more of a complex chemical distillery than an animal, it's a scientific miracle that it doesn’t explode every time it coughs. Surprisingly effective in combat in ways the enemy would really have preferred not knowing.

A humanoid hybrid with recessive boomalope genes. Thanks to its sac filled wit

creatures.label: shock goat

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: Shock goats are domesticated cattle, renowned for their capacity to store static electricity on their bony structures, and releasing it as a defensive measure. Interestingly enough, the shock goat has characteristics common to many other Rim species, such as three pairs of eyes, and characteristics typical of Earth goats, such as the horns. This points to the conclusion that shock goats are actual

creatures.label: angel moth

evidence.why: eats a substance no animal should
produces <AA_MothSilk> — not a normal animal product

creatures.label: maxolotl
creatures.desc: These large salamanders prefer wet environments with pools of water they can comfortably slip into. While they lack teeth, their strong jaws can crush the shells of most insects. They are capable of fertilizing multiple batches of eggs in one go.

creatures.label: tibidee
creatures.desc: Tibidees were giant silicon-based creature native to Stygeon Prime, though they could also be found on other mountainous Outer Rim planets (such as Oosalon). Though normally gentle, tibidees would attack anything they felt was threatening.

creatures.label: angel moth larva
creatures.desc:
Angel moths are beautiful lepidopterans that undergo metamorphosis, similar to other more mundane moths. Angel moths are yet another example of a genetically engineered project of waste disposal being abandoned, and its subjects being released into the wild.

creatures.label: Boar-wolf
creatures.desc: The boar-wolves (or 'Borra'), were a predatory animal that came from the forest moon of Endor. Boar-wolves were believed to be closer to wolves than boars physiologically speaking, and usually hunted for prey such as blurrgs. They could be trained as attack beasts and so have been exported to various worlds by criminal elements for such purposes.

creatures.label: sacapillar
creatures.desc: Timid by nature, this larva-like bug has a large thorax filled with putrescent gasses, allowing it to move about and escape attackers while barely touching the ground. It releases these gasses when attacked, often allowing it to escape unharmed. The gasses it contains also permit it to carry large loads, and many colonies in polluted areas use them as ridable pack animals.

creatures.label: mantistanis
creatures.desc:
Mixing the genes of one of the biggest carnivorous birds ever existing and those of a praying mantis is either a genious idea, or anathema. The Mantistanis stalks its prey by standing incredibly still and launching itself to attack with lightning speed.

Gigantic hyena-like predators. Their exceptionally strong jaws easily crush bones.
Extremely aggresive, it's known to surprisingly often prey on animals larger than itself.

creatures.label: macrauchenia
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Despite it possessing a trunk, macrauchenia's nostrils are actually located on the top of its head.
It's extraordinarily agile and thanks to its ability of rapidly changing directions while running at high speed, it can escape most predators fairly easily.

creatures.label: uintatherium
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

A very primitive, giant cousin of rhinoceroses.
It is neither the most beautiful, nor the most intelligent animal in history, with its brain being merely the size of an orange, but it can make up for it with its strong back, which renders it a good partner for a journey.

creatures.label: sivatherium
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The biggest ruminant in history. Unlike its modern equivalents, giraffes and okapis, sivatherium possesses two pairs of ossicones, one that is wide and resembles antlers, and the other being more horn-like, placed above its eyes.

creatures.desc:
Atispecs are strange semi-insectoid creatures that undergo a radical metamorphosis, similar to old terran butterflies. In their larval phase, atispecs are basically harmless: a medium-sized grub that feeds on plants and usually ends up as some predator's meal. Tens of thousands of atispec larvae hatch every season, and less than a dozen make it to their adult form.

creatures.desc:
The Animus Hare is a small leporid with latent psionic abilities. Quite intelligent for an animal, but not intelligent enough to properly use psionics. It will however quickly bond with human beings and reach with his mind to make happy everyone that treats it well.

Useful abilities: they will often use a psionic nuzzle on colonists, keeping everyone happier. They also breed very fast.

creatures.label: royal megascarab
creatures.desc: A medium-sized naturally-evolved insectoid the size of a sheep. Being part of the royal hive, these larger megascarabs act as a worker caste of the primary hives, and are always seen serving around the hive leaders. creatures.label: tauntaun
creatures.desc: Tauntauns are a species of omnivorous reptomammals who are indigenous to the icy planet of Hoth. Tauntauns were commonly used as pack animals during the Rebel Alliance's stay at Hoth. Tauntauns were also used as patrol mounts when it was learned that the Rebel Alliance's own vehicles could not cope with the very cold weather.

creatures.label: royal ave
creatures.desc: Royal Aves are large flightless birds with colourful feathers. Royal Aves were originally wild Meadow Aves that have been cross-bred for generations to reduce their stubbornness and increase their fluffiness. Long extinct giant arthropods, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The biggest land scorpion to ever exist.
Pulmonoscorpius is a solitary predator capable of taking down creatures way larger than itself with its deadly venom. Its sting should be stayed away from at all costs.

creatures.desc:
The animal we’ve all been waiting for, namely one that not only cleans up after itself but for others as well. Their fur is surprisingly soft and has antibacterial properties, which it uses along with its fingered paws to clean surfaces. Once the fur starts to become matted is when it needs to be trimmed.

A muffalo hybrid with recessive humanoid genes. Quite intelligent but they lose out on a lot

creatures.label: nerf
creatures.desc: Nerfs were a species of furry, non-sentient animals raised for their milk, meat, and hide. They could be found on a variety of planets across the galaxy, from Alderaan to Lothal. Despite their usefulness, nerfs were often regarded as disgusting because of their strong body odor.

creatures.label: blurrg
creatures.desc: Blurrgs were a two-legged non-sentient reptilian species that were used as beasts of burden on a number of worlds located across the galaxy. Blurrgs had two short arms that had two fingers with claws, and a thick tail that helped them balance. creatures.label: splicehulk
creatures.desc:
A swollen bloated mutant that quivers with every labored step. Its skin splits under its own weight, oozing yellow fluid from raw seams. Vaguely resembling what was once a human, its limbs of mismatched size flail clumsily at anything nearby. Somehow, it’s able to regenerate all wounds at an unnatural speed.

While slow and ponderous, its immense bulk crushes obstacles with ease leaving little hop

creatures.label: alpha thrumbo
creatures.desc:
A gigantic, graceful creature of unknown origin. Alpha thrumbos are even rarer and more dangerous than the typical thrumbo. Their hide is nearly impossible to pierce and their razor-sharp horn is worth more than its weight in gold.

Alpha thrumbos are some of the longest-lived moving creatures in the known universe. Some tribes believe they remember and psychically pass on everything they ever exp

creatures.label: thrumbear
creatures.desc:
If you thought Thrumbos were tough and hit like a tank, may I present to you the answer to all your prayers. If you can feed the thing, this absolute unit would work extremely well as an assault force against any force foolish enough to threaten its feedstock. Plus you get to ride it on long journeys, possibly clearing entire forests on the way.

A colossal hybrid with recessive ursine genes. Whil

creatures.label: guinea pig
creatures.desc: Neither a pig or a creature from Guinea, these little rodents are bred to be a household pet and a delicious dinner.

creatures.label: quail
creatures.desc: Small plump ground-dwelling birds with a distinctive plume.

creatures.label: clodhopper
creatures.desc: Clodhoppers were omnivorous and dim-witted flightless avians from the planet Naboo but could be found as castaway populations on numerous worlds due to illegal egg exports. Clodhopper weren't large creatures, but they fed in swarms becoming a real menace to agriculture. They were protected by tough, durable skin. Fast-breeding, dimwitted, voracious grazers, clodhoppers would use their powerful for

creatures.label: Scavrats
creatures.desc: Scavrats were large, omnivorous rodents of unknown planetary origin albeit common enough on multiple worlds that they were considered pests. They were often mistaken for the Tattooinian Womp Rat, but the big behavioural distinction here being that they were not predatory and far more sociable creatures despite their strange appearance.

creatures.label: Grank
creatures.desc: The Grank (or 'saw-toothed grank') were a medium-sized carnivore believed to have originated on the planet Naboo. They were a species of predatory scavengers with sharp teeth and powerful jaws. Despite their fearsome gnarled appearance they were very affectionate when domesticated. This made them popular pets and lead to them establishing wild populations on multiple worlds as a result.

creatures.label: alpaca
creatures.desc: A medium-sized ungulate closely related to the llama, the alpaca is usually raised for its remarkably soft and insulating wool. Alpacas have also been used as pack animals since they hauled cargo on the rugged mountain trails of ancient South America.

creatures.label: kybuck
creatures.desc: Kybucks were bipedal ungulates native to the planet Kashyyyk, and similar in appearance to the tauntauns of Hoth. These herding pack animals were fast and sociable, which made domestication and export offworld common.

creatures.label: qormot
creatures.desc: Qormots were omnivorous forest creatures from the planet Yeshocq. During the mating season their ferocity increased, usually making anyone bold (or foolish) enough to stray into Qormot territory a likely target. However, much to the dismay of the game hunters who exported these creatures to various worlds, their seasonal aggression diminished heavily when transplanted.

creatures.label: meadow ave
creatures.desc:
A large flightless bird with colorful feathers. Mostly found in the plains eating fruits and berries, Meadow Aves naturally attract the eyes and hands of those who wander by. Many forget that underneath the majestic feathery coat is a wild animal with a razor sharp beak and claws to match.

Meadow Aves are amazing mounts, much faster than horses, and if properly trained they can be ridden into bat

creatures.label: gnaut
creatures.desc:
Gnauts are large grazing animals, robust and social, reminiscent of ancient wildebeest and wild bovine stock. They live well in herds and fit naturally into open ecosystems, turning ordinary vegetation into meat, hide, bones and horns.

They provide no milk or wool, but make up for it through simplicity: domesticable animals useful to colonies that need a stable source of resources without relying

creatures.label: runyip
creatures.desc: Runyip or Yavin Runyip were a species of squat quadrupeds from the moon Yavin 4. The creatures had antlered heads with a flexible nose. Their coats had a characteristic pattern of black or dark brown stripes on a whitish background. It is believed this striation made them a popular game animal for export to other worlds.

creatures.label: giant toad
creatures.desc: A truly giant amphibian, this fearsome creature has hind legs that are mounds of pure muscle, allowing it to race horses and come out on top. Their skin is hard, leathery and bumpy, marked by islets of darker coulouration. Their enormous throat sacs let them call mates and make threats that can be heard over many miles. Their tongues shoot out at bullet speed when pursuing prey, be it large flies

creatures.label: jimvu
creatures.desc: The jimvu were native to the grasslands of the planet Naboo. The jimvu was an agile, six-legged, ungulate-like reptile whose best defense was its swiftness. Their main predators were the veermok and narglatch. They were exported as a prey species on various worlds where typically large predators where hunted for sport.

creatures.label: shaak
creatures.desc: Shaaks were plump pachydermoid herd animals native to the planet of Naboo. Shaaks were often raised for their meat, and had large, rotund bodies. Due to their high rate of reproduction they were often sold offworld in livestock markets.

creatures.label: taraal
creatures.desc:
The taraal, also known as great land owl is a huge omnivorous bird that dwells in the many forests of the world. They primarily eat fish, and can be often seen near rivers and lakes in search of their favourite prey. In its absence, the taraal will not hesitate to use its immense, bear-like strength to hunt live prey instead..

When the wind grows cold and the first snows begin, taraals leave thei

creatures.label: dalgo
creatures.desc: Dalgos were equine reptiles native to the planet of Onderon. Despite being carnivorous predators, they could still be domesticated and filled the same role as other beasts of burden. It is for this reason these creatures found themselves spread across many worlds.

creatures.label: hrumph
creatures.desc: The hrumphs were powerful, thick-necked herbivores native to planet Naboo, but also found on other worlds like Aargonar. Hrumphs received their name from the loud, deep, guttural sounds they produced. They had four long horns for defense and for the protection of their two long, sensitive ears. They were not choosy about their food which made them hardy enough to survive on many other worlds.

creatures.label: bolotaur
creatures.desc: The Bolotaur are a large, long-necked herbivorous reptilian creatures native to the planet Kashyyyk. They were short-lived but reproduced quickly and were a favoured mount by the Trandoshan species, which resulted in their spread to many worlds as beasts of burden and livestock.

creatures.label: falumpaset
creatures.desc: The falumpaset were a large mammalalian creature native to the planet Naboo. Their distinctive bellowing calls could be heard for kilometers around and their intelligence made them likely to form strong bonds with their handlers. Easily domesticated as beasts of burden (or sometimes war mounts), falumpasets could be found all over the galaxy.

creatures.label: gundark
creatures.desc: Gundarks were fearsome anthropoids from the planet Vanqor. They were known as one of the most vicious, strong, and aggressive species in the galaxy. This ferocity resulted in them being exported across to many worlds as gladiatorial combatants or as exotic pets. They had two powerful arms used in combat and locomotion, two smaller arms for manipulation and walked on a specialised single clawed-toe

creatures.label: tusk cat
creatures.desc: The tusk cat were large feline predators from the worlds of Naboo and its moon Rori. Tusk cats had a large pair of distinct tusks growing from their lower jaws. This put them at morphological odds with many tusked animals which often featured tusks growing from the upper jaw. A second, less-noticeable pair of tusk-like fleshy appendages grew from their cheekbones. Despite their predatory nature, t

creatures.label: megasquid
creatures.desc: The megasquid is a large omnivorous terasquid. Heavier than an elephant and almost as tall, a megasquid lumbers through the forest, moving at speeds similar to a human's walking pace.

creatures.label: landopus
creatures.desc: Despite the name, this bad-tempered creature evolved from squid and has eight tentacles and two arms. The landopus has a venomous bite and a full load of its deadly neurotoxin will kill a healthy adult human in a minute or less.

creatures.label: convor
creatures.desc: Convor (also known as "Trandoshan birds"), were a species of beautiful mammavian from the Wasskah moon of Hsskhor. Although Convor had short, plump bodies, they were excellent fliers. Their popularity as a pet meant they often established colonies on other worlds.

creatures.label: gullipud
creatures.desc: Gullipuds were bulky, loose-skinned, self-inflating amphibians native to the swamps of the planet Naboo. As they were small and easy prey for other animals, like pikobis, gullipuds would extend their spine to make themselves harder to catch and swallow. Due to their physical similarities to the more common gorg these creatures may have been unintentionally transported to various worlds as livestoc

creatures.label: yobshrimp
creatures.desc: Yobshrimp were a carnivorous crustacean native to the shallow waters of the planet Naboo. These clawed creatures were typically preyed upon by animals such as Blarths and larger scalefish. Some considered this animal a delicacy and many fishing families cultivated the yobshrimp for consumption which resulted in it's dispersal to various worlds.

creatures.label: shiro
creatures.desc: Shiros were hard-shelled, benign, slow-moving reptiles native to the planet of Naboo. A Shiro's main defense was to retract its head, legs and tail into its spiny shell. The Shiro's low metabolism meant it could be transported over long journeys and understandably the species was spread to many worlds.

creatures.label: nuna
creatures.desc: Nuna (commonly called 'swamp turkeys'), were reptavian gamebirds native to the planet Naboo. Nuna were diminutive bipeds, mostly covered in scaly skin and sporting a distinctive dorsal ridge. They possessed a notably prominent jutting jaw and two large wattles hanging from either side of their mouths. They were transported as livestock as well as a game animal, allowing for wild populations on oth

creatures.label: ollopom
creatures.desc: Ollopoms were squat, gentle herbivores native to the swamps of the planet Naboo. A species of six-legged aquatic rodent, they were often mistaken for water plants. These short, gentle, dense, green-furred rodents were camouflaged to blend in with the Pom Petals whose edges they fed upon. On their underside, they had gnawing teeth and three pairs of paddle-like claws. Their flukes were used as rudd

creatures.label: mott
creatures.desc: Motts were medium sized, semi-aquatic herbivores native to the swamps of Naboo. They ate a wide variety of vegetation and were a primary source of food for most swamp predators. Fortunately, motts had a high reproduction rate.

creatures.label: shiro-trap
creatures.desc: The Shiro-trap was native to planet Naboo and was not entirely a separate creature, but in fact a symbiotic pairing of a Tooke-trap plant and a Shiro. The plant disguised the animal, while the Shiro provided the plant a form of locomotion. creatures.label: cephalope
creatures.desc: Descended from squid this tentacled monstrosity is like a spider the size of a deer. Fast and aggressive with a lethal bite delivered by venomous beak. An internal shell protects their vital organs.

creatures.label: kaadu
creatures.desc: Kaadu were large, flightless reptavians that inhabited the swamps of the planets Naboo, Obredaan as well as the moon of Rori. They had sharp hearing and a keen sense of smell and adults of the species had distinct markings to distinguish gender. Kaadu were known to be fearless; consequently many were domesticated as steeds during times of conflict, or as patrol animals. This versatility made them

creatures.label: boma
creatures.desc: Bomas were ravenous beasts native to planet Onderon and its moon Dxun. In their native environment they hunted Cannoks with ease and were considered dangerous by several Mandalorian clans. They were sometimes introduced into ecosystems on other worlds where Cannoks had become established to help maintain their population.

creatures.label: fanback
creatures.desc: The fanback was a cold-blooded predatory amphibian from the swamps of Naboo. Each fanback had a big dorsal spine along with a sensitive snout which allowed them to hunt for fish and other small free swimming prey with ease. creatures.label: Peko-peko
creatures.desc: Peko-pekos were large colourful reptavians whose raucous squawks that carried over long distances. They were native to the Gungan swamps of the planet Naboo, but another breed was known to live on Nal Hutta. creatures.label: hssiss
creatures.desc: Hssiss (or "dark side dragons") were a poisnous reptile native to the planet Ambria. They were slow but aggressive ambush predators that preferred to live near bodies of water. Hssiss could be found all over the galaxy, especially on worlds where the "dark side" was strong (with most being descended from those brought by the many historical "Sith" armies).

creatures.label: silooth
creatures.desc: The silooth were a large 'Sithspawn' acid spitting beetle bred by the Sith Empire for use as a warbeast. Silooth were ferocious creatures using their powerful mandibles to crush their prey or tear down trees and buildings. Legends tell of one such creature that has grown so large and so powerful that it had entir

creatures.label: thranta
creatures.desc: Thrantas were a group of flying animals originally found on the planet Alderaan. While there were multiple species and breeds varying in size and functions, most thrantas served as air transport. Populations of wild thranta were established on numerous worlds (like Bespin) where the air pollution was low.

creatures.label: kowakian monkey-lizard

creatures.desc: Kowakian monkey-lizards were a bipedal reptillian primate species native to a jungle-like Outer Rim planet called Kowak. Their intelligence and cunning made them popular exports as exotic pets, with some specimens escaping and establishing wild colonies.

creatures.label: monkey
creatures.desc: A small primate, the monkey can use its curly tail to grab on to branches, leaving its hands free to do other things. Monkeys are selfish but clever, and can be trained to carry out fairly complex tasks.

creatures.label: Borcatu

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: Borcatu were small, bad-tempered scavengers originally found on the planet of Escabar. Borcatu had a scaly, thick hide which may have evolved to help resist sandstorms. They also have sharp teeth, claws and quills to defend themselves. They had a vicious temperament, biting anyone who came near them, and often fighting and cannibalizing one another when no other food source was available. Their ha

creatures.label: whisperbird
creatures.desc: Whisper birds were energetic avians native to the moon Yavin 4. They were known for their radiant plumage and gained their name due to their seemingly noiseless flight. They used their dexterous tongue to emit their sweet, low-pitched song or call. These traits made them popular pets with avian enthausiasts and wild populations soon appeared from escapees on numerous worlds (even on polluted world

creatures.label: stintaril
creatures.desc: The stintarils were a species of rapacious arboreal rodents native to the moon Yavin 4. They were predators and their prey mainly consisted of woolamanders and whisper birds, but could and would hunt other small to medium sized creatures. The metabolism of the stintaril was extremely high, and they had to eat often. It's very likely these voracious predators were introduced and established themsel

creatures.label: tach
creatures.desc: The tach were a species tree-dwelling primates native to the planet Kashyyyk. A friendly creature, the tach could often be found on the ground searching for overripe fruits. They were exported to various worlds by unscrupulous business enterprises harvest their brain glands for use in the production of expensive Tarisian ale.

creatures.label: iriaz
creatures.desc: Iriaz were docile creatures from the grassland planet Dantooine. While not normally aggressive, they could attack if provoked. They were a prey of choice for local hunters (and natural predators alike) given that they were a relatively common creature; furthering their export to many planets.

creatures.label: woolamander
creatures.desc: Woolamanders were curious social creatures that originated on the jungle moon of Yavin 4. They fed on fruit and other vegetation that would ferment in their pot-bellies. Colouful primate often made for exotic pets and these sociable animals were spread to multiple worlds where upon escaping wild populations soon established themselves.

creatures.label: zarander
creatures.desc: The zarander is a large elephant-like suine. Despite its large trunk, it has little sense of smell. It relies on keen hearing to detect predators.

creatures.label: cannok
creatures.desc: Cannoks were small, aggressive predators native to the moon of Dxun. They had a habit of eating anything that could fit in their mouths and were known as pests, due to a high reproduction rate and notable curiosity. Cannoks were however hardy and able to survive the rigors of many worlds.

creatures.label: yippa
creatures.desc: A long necked lama-like herbivore. Native to tropical climates. The upper layers of vegetation are exploited by the yippa.

creatures.label: panther
creatures.desc: An agile and powerful big cat native to the jungles of old Earth. As solitary ambush predators, panthers are masters of taking down both large and small prey. Onlookers tend to focus on their graceful movements, while those in closer contact usually notice their skull-crushing strength.

creatures.label: kinrath

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc: Kinrath were a species of large, non-sentient arachnoids found on Dantooine, Kashyyyk, and several other planets. Kinrath had four legs and a leg-like, poisonous appendage coming out of their faces that they used to attack prey or other perceived enemies. All kinrath were blind but could sense heat which allowed them to navigate their way around and identify potential threats.

creatures.label: can-cell
creatures.desc: Can-cells were a species of scavenging flying insectoids found on a number of planets across the galaxy (although it is believed they originated on Kashyyk). Can-Cells evolved many of their strange physical characteristics to maximise their survival in the dangerous forests and jungles they inhabit.

creatures.label: Bernicia
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #0244439-1927 [BERNICIA PRAECURSOR] CODENAME: SHELL >355

Slow and friendly, these big extinct snails are a cute - albeit slimy - addition to any colony. Looking past their incredibly slow speed, these gastropod wonders have insanely strong shells, and can secrete a ruddy copper paste that, when dried, can be used as a hard plastic.

creatures.label: Manipulator
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #08362-2015 [MANIPULATOR MODIFICAPUTIS] CODENAME: MANTIS >645

An extinct predatory cockroach altered to massive proportions. It is an ancestor to modern day mantids, and acts similarly, with large, grasping legs to grapple prey.

creatures.label: gutkurr
creatures.desc: Gutkurrs were fierce insectile predators native to the planet Ryloth. They were aggressive and displayed very limited intelligence, however they were observed to work in small hunting packs. These traits however has made them popular game animals and "pets" for criminal organisations across the galaxy, spreading these monsterous creatures to many worlds.

creatures.label: insectomorph
creatures.desc: Insectomorphs were insectoids from the planet Malastare. These easily domesticated omnivores were often used by the Dugs on their homeworld as battle mounts. Despite their unusual appearance they have been able to flourish as livestock on multiple worlds due to their rapid growth and hardiness.

creatures.label: mastiff phalone
creatures.desc: Mastiff phalone were carnivorous flightless avians native to the savannas of Maridun. The mastiff phalones had turkey-like heads with a sharp beak and a mane of large brown feathers which males of the species used in courtship displays. Mastiff phalones descended from flying creatures, with their wings evolved back into powerful limbs and tended to hunt in packs of two to four. They were popular b

creatures.label: vornskyr

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc: The vornskr were a pack hunting canine beast native to the forest planet Myrkr. Vornskrs were primarily nocturnal hunters, and used their whip-like, mildly venomous tails to stun prey before finishing it off with their teeth. They were popular attack beasts and pets within several criminal organisations and thus they were spread to numerous worlds as a result.

creatures.label: gelagrub
creatures.desc: Gelagrubs, also known as 'Felucian ground beetles', were large insectine creatures native to Felucia. This variety (with some genetic tweaking) found themselves popular for export to many Rimworlds because they remained in their useful grub-like state for their entire lives whilst also swapping out their normal phosphorescence for neutroamine production.

creatures.label: devourer
creatures.desc: Devourers were carnivorous anthropoids twisted by the dark side of the Force that were indigenous to jungle moon of Dxun. Devourers were known across many worlds for having attacked (and in some instances killed) several notable figures in galactic history who wandered into their territory. They were fierce creatures and were sometimes exported as attack animals to other worlds where escaped speci

creatures.label: acklay
creatures.desc: The acklay is a non-sentient carnivore native to planet Vendaxa. Acklays have sharp claws, thick skin, and are about 3 meters tall. Due to these attributes, as well as the species' ferocity, acklays are often exported from Vendaxa to be used in gladiatorial combat. The creatures can be found on Geonosis, where they are commonly brought in to fight other creatures—and sentients—in the Petranaki are

creatures.label: Kwi
creatures.desc: The Kwi were large, bipedal saurians native to the planet Dathomir. They were herbivorous and yet remarkably sociable and intelligent. They were believed to be the degenerated descendants of the saurian 'Kwa' race. How they arrived on the various worlds they populated is unknown; perhaps they are the long descendants of the pan-galactic 'Kwa' or maybe they are just escaped circus specimens.

creatures.label: rhinoceros
creatures.desc: Despite being herbivorous, this large mammal is very easy to enrage. Once angered, its massive strength and sharp horn make it a brutal opponent. It has more muscle in one leg than most humans do in their whole body.

creatures.label: titanis
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant birds, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Colloquially known as terror birds, titanis are large carnivorous flightless birds. Their abnormally huge beaks are incredibly deadly, and their strong legs not only allow them to easily outrun their prey, but can also serve vicious kicks.

creatures.label: varactyl
creatures.desc: Varactyls, also known as 'dragonmounts', were reptavian herbivores native to the planet Utapau, though some specimens found their way to other worlds (such as Kashyyyk and Belsavis) as their eggs were easily transported by Black-marketeers. They had beaked faces and long, powerful tails and not only could a varactyl run very fast, but their feet were adapted with tiny hairlike structures that allo

creatures.label: wyyyschokk
creatures.desc: Wyyyschokk were a species of gigantic spider that lived on the planet Kashyyyk. Both highly intelligent and extremely hostile, they could ensnare prey by casting webbing at them.

creatures.label: arthropleura
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant arthropods, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest known land invertebrate of all time. Arthropleuras are huge, solitary, herbivorous millipedes that are mostly harmless, and will attack only in self-defense.
Some maniacs are willing to pay unreasonable amounts of money for eggs of this beast.

creatures.label: corinathoth
creatures.desc: Corinathoths were large, slow-moving herbivores native to the planet Maridun. Although large and intimidating, they were fairly harmless unless provoked. It is likely they were spread as a large game animal to several worlds due to their fearsome appearance.

creatures.label: elephant
creatures.desc:
The largest unmodified land animal. Elephants have a long trunk they use to manipulate objects, and sharp tusks they use to gore attackers. A dead elephant's valuable tusks can be recovered by butchering it.

Intelligent creatures with complex social relationships, elephants can be used as pack animals or trained to carry out the most complex of tasks. They live a long time, and are known to remem

creatures.label: giantala
creatures.desc: A large ground sloth-like marsupial that lives in the undergrowth of the tropical forests. Its giant tail acts as an extra leg to help it stand upright.

creatures.label: katarn
creatures.desc: A katarn was a predatory quadruped reptomammal native to the planet Kashyyyk. Katarns had slender bodies with rodent-like tails, and narrow faces leading back to a cartilaginous ridge protecting their neck and shoulders. Katarns were creatures of great importance in the Wookiees' culture. The Wookiees, who called the katarn the "Old Prince", hunted them in their hrrtayyk ceremony. They were a popu

creatures.label: vapaad

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc: The vapaad, was a large predatory creature native to the world of Sarapin and its moons. Vaapads were brown ball-shaped, tripod creatures with two yellow eyes and multiple tentacles used to kill prey. A vaapad attacked by striking its prey with its toxic tentacles so quickly that they were nothing but a blur to the naked eye. They were exported offworld for use in exotic gladiatorial arenas.

creatures.label: ithorian reek
creatures.desc: Reek could be found on the planets Iridonia, Kashyyyk, Ithor, Codian Moon, Tatooine and Saleucami (to name just a few). Various subspecies invariably sprung up as the base stock adapted to new environments. The Ithorian Reek were used as plow animals by the Ithorians and were larger and stronger than those found on Ylesia. Their horns were also smaller because of the lack of hostility between this

creatures.label: Arthropleura
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #0291-1933 [ARTHROPLEURA ARMATA] CODENAME: MYRIA >437

A herbivorous arthropod that can reach gigantic proportions. They often eat low lying shrubbery and decaying leaves, rummaging through the undergrowth. They are weak and easy to hunt, but their meat is undersirable.

creatures.label: harvester beetle
creatures.desc: The harvester beetle were a large domesticated insectoid native to the planet Neimoidia, but were transplanted to all the Neimoidian purse worlds (as well as potential) worlds. They were large, herbivorous and were able to carry heavy loads on their swept backs. In the absence of their 'hive queens' pheremones, these animals have become feral but they still make excellent beasts of burden and can

creatures.label: torton
creatures.desc: Tortons were huge predatory estudines that were believed to have originated on Naboo's moon of Rori, but identical such specimens existed on other worlds such as the Tortur from the planet Talus. Their tough shells made them formidable foes in angered, however their bulk made them slow and cumbersome.

creatures.label: zakkeg
creatures.desc: Zakkegs were rare alpha-predators indigenous to the moon of Dxun. They were huge, armoured quadrupeds, typically solitary and territorial. Even Mandalorians were impressed by someone who killed one, and one could gain great honor for proving one's success. Due to this, several Mandalorian clans and big game hunters exported these creatures to numerous worlds to provide a ready supply of the beasts

creatures.label: k'lor'slug

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc: K'lor'slugs were poisonous vermiforms native to the swamps of planet Noe'ha'on, but could be found in sizable populations on other worlds (including Korriban and Taris). They were known to invade the darkest spots on unsanitary space vehicles and breed (aiding in their spread to new planets). Because of their notoriety as an aggressive and deadly species (especially among the spacers who encounter

creatures.label: veermok
creatures.desc: Veermoks were a ferocious species of clawed and fanged primates native to the planet Naboo (but with sizeable populations on both Eriadau and Xirl). Living in swamps and moist woodlands, veermoks were arboreal creatures. They were also solitary and aggressive creatures, spending the majority of their lives without others of their kind. Their popularity amongst big game hunters meant they were expo

creatures.label: blixus
creatures.desc: Blixus were rare, half-shelled crustapod creatures native to the planet Sljee. These semi-aquatic predators were known to be deadly in the swamps and lagoons they inhabit. They were known to periodically shed their exoskeleton if broken or damaged which could be harvested for useful chitin. It is believed many were accidently transplanted to various worlds as exotic display animals or pets that gr

creatures.label: dianoga
creatures.desc: Dianoga originated on the planet Vodran and were large cephalopods capable of growing to great sizes. They had a single eyestalk protruding from their mollusk-like bodies, and seven suckered tentacles surrounding a fanged maw containing a sharp serrated probe. Normally these creatures were restricted to bodies of water, but this variety seems just as comfortable dragging itself around on land.

creatures.label: Dragonsnake
creatures.desc: The dragonsnake (also spelled 'dragon snake') were a large, semi-aquatic predatory reptiles that dwelled in the muddy waters of various planets, including Dagobah and Nal Hutta. Dragonsnakes were large serpentlike beasts with sharp fangs and biolumescent spots along their backs. Although voracious, they were incapable of digesting metal (a lucky escape for some heroic droids!). The dragonsnake "Br

creatures.label: kell dragon
creatures.desc: Kell dragons (also known as 'kell drakes') were were hardy, thick skinned creatures from the mountainous planet Rinderga. They were related to the much larger krayt dragons indigenous to Tatooine, but unlike their larger cousins were comfortable in both deserts and tundra. Kell dragons were believed to have been chemically altered by Sith Alchemy from the original krayt stock for use as effective

creatures.label: kwazel maw
creatures.desc: Kwazel Maw were giant aquatic slugs from the planet Rodia. They were a slow predatory creatures with remarkably tough hides that relied on ambush. Despite naturally inhabiting swamps, it appeared Kwazel Maw were equally comfortable on land. Their presence on other planets remains a mystery, although it is speculated that the eggs of these creatures may have been sold offworld as form of 'caviar' b

creatures.label: fambaa
creatures.desc: Fambaas were large herbivorous amphibians most often found in swamps. Fambaas were technically amphibians but had the scaly hide of reptiles. The creatures size and usefulness when domesticated meant they were exported to many worlds as beasts of burden.

creatures.label: nautilant
creatures.desc: These armored behemoths are ambush predators, using their powerful tentacles to snatch prey and deliver a venomous bite. Their limestone shells are self-contained ecosystems of stored water and symbiotic algae that can keep the enormous mollusc alive in almost any environment.

creatures.label: hare
creatures.desc: This small, solitary herbivore can swiftly hop away from danger.

creatures.label: snowhare
creatures.desc: This hardy animal survives the brutal winters of its homelands by burrowing through snow to find edible plants.

creatures.label: caribou
creatures.desc: A large member of the deer family, well-adapted to life in cold climates. Caribou can be milked, but refuse to carry packs.

creatures.label: ibex
creatures.desc: The wild ancestor of the domesticated goat. Ibexes live on marginal territory where most antelopes couldn't survive, eating lichens and sparse mountain plants. They're famous for dextrously hopping across bare cliff faces - and for their violent ramming attack.

creatures.label: elk
creatures.desc: A large member of the deer family, well-adapted to life in cold climates. Domesticated elk can be milked, but refuse to carry packs.

creatures.label: chameleon yak

evidence.why: mod wrote custom C# pawn class
produces a SEASONAL product that changes with the biome: AA_ChameleonYakWoolTemperate, AA_ChameleonYakWoolWinter, AA_ChameleonYakWoolJungle, AA_ChameleonYakWoolDesert

creatures.desc:
The Chameleon Yak is a long-haired domesticated bovid that has evolved a fascinating survival mechanism involving camouflage, similar to the way a chameleon changes its skin colour in response to different stimuli. The Chameleon Yak takes this a step further, changing its very metabolism according to the environment it is inhabiting at the time.

Chameleon Yaks will change their temperature tolera

creatures.label: aminox
creatures.desc:
Aminox are huge cold-climate herbivores descended from ancient muskox-like lineages. Their thick coats and natural endurance let them survive across tundras, frozen plains and regions where ordinary cattle would not last long.

The true value of the Aminox lies in its milk. Dense, nutritious and rich in unusual amino compounds, it sustains colonies in extreme environments and serves as the basis f

creatures.label: manka
creatures.desc: Manka (or 'manka cats') were a large predatory feline species native to the planets Tython and Alderaan. Fur-covered quad-tusked quadrupeds, 'manka cats' were considered dangerous by most sentients who encountered them and were often hunted for safety reasons as well as for resources (their tusks were known to have unusual curative properties). Manka cat populations were present on numerous worlds

creatures.label: bantha
creatures.desc: Banthas are a species of large, hairy mammals with sharp, spiraling horns. They inhabit the desert planet Tatooine, though they are bred on many worlds throughout the galaxy. They are social herd animals, and are often domesticated, and used prominently, by Tusken Raiders as mounts and companionship.

creatures.label: crestel

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
One of the largest flightless birds, and the north's apex predator. The crestel is a fearsome beast that can completely paralyze unfortunate victims for a short duration with its venomous beak, rendering them helpless against its attacks. Despite their delicate look, the crestel's feathers are harder than stone, serving as natural armor.

Its vicious nature and unusual appearance perpetuates numer

creatures.label: shimmershell snail

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <BMT_HermaphroditicAnimal> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: Similar to the other gigantic snail species found underground and on Caveworlds, this species has been modified to bioluminesce.

creatures.label: pikobis
creatures.desc: Pikobi were fast-moving, flightless reptavians which were native to the swamps of Naboo and the jungles of Onderon. Pikobis also had long, pointed beaks lined with sharp teeth that were used to spear and hold onto slippery prey which it usually swallowed in one gulp. Due to their small size they were often able to hide as stowaways aboard large cargo ships, surviving by scavenging and escaping to

creatures.label: xyrion
creatures.desc: This large reptile was first brought to Rimworlds as a strange pet due to its ability to lose its tail without harm, much like some geckos. Years after some were released or escaped into underground caverns, their preferred habitat, it was discovered that they can be raised and farmed for their surprisingly nutritious tails. Their tails begin to grow back immedately after removal but take days to

creatures.label: amaro
creatures.desc: An awakened species of feathered reptiles made incredibly intelligent through glitterworld genetic engineering and selective breeding. With a lifespan comparable to humans and slow birth rate, they make for a singular lifelong riding companion. Rumours state that those that have been in the presence of humans for long periods learn how to speak, but those are followed by such creatures being whisk

creatures.label: ripper hound

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
Ripper Hounds were created as a purely biological defense against Insectoids, a genetically engineered species bred for hunting and defeating them. These hulking canines sport two viciously sharp claws specially designed to attach to chitinous plates and rip them apart.

Despite their fearsome appearance, Ripper Hounds can be extremely affectionate and loyal, and they love to be pet by those they

creatures.label: thunderbeast

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch
Alpha Animals flags this creature as having a ranged attack

creatures.desc:
The thunderbeast is a swine-like mammal capable of generating large electric currents by way of a highly specialized nervous system that has the capacity to synchronize the activity of disc-shaped, electricity-producing cells packed into a specialized electric organ.

Though they were initially created to serve as a way to generate bio-electricity similarly to Tetra slugs, thunderbeasts have natur

creatures.label: megabat
creatures.desc: This massive species of bat has become largely flightless, instead walking on its wings. It has learned to use its echolocation as a weapon to disorient prey.

creatures.label: ironhusk beetle

evidence.why: produces <Steel> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
Ironhusk beetles were genetically engineered by one of the myriad mining companies operating on the Rim. It's a peaceful farm animal that occasionally sheds metallic husks that can be used as steel, thus negating the need for heavy machinery in mining operations. As a downside, the beetle consumes a huge amount of wood from live trees.

Sadly, the mining company that created the Ironhusk beetles d

creatures.label: giant snail

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <BMT_HermaphroditicAnimal> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: A gigantic herd snail used as a pack animal by many cavern-dwelling societies. Its ability to adhere to and climb virtually any surface makes it invaluable for traders or travelers underground.

creatures.label: sludgecrawler

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <BMT_HermaphroditicAnimal> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: A gigantic mutant snail with two heads. It uses its unique slime for defense, as it rapidly hardens into something akin to biological cement.

creatures.label: wolfhorse
creatures.desc: Combining two of the most renowned endurance hunters in human history has resulted in man’s best friend whom you can also ride into battle with. Needless to say, the creation of this capricious canine was celebrated by many wealthy families who otherwise caused unfortunate accidents when they tried to ride their household dog when they clearly became too old or heavy for them to carry. What was no

creatures.label: skalder
creatures.desc: The skalder were a mammalian desert species of herbivorous quadrupeds native to the plains of the planet Florrum. They were not normally ridden by sentient beings, but were surprisingly fast if such a feat was managed. They made exceptional pack animals, even in toxic environments and so were exported by pirate bands for use offworld.

creatures.label: tuk'ata

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc: The tuk'ata (or 'Sith hounds'), were used for thousands of years to guard the tombs of the Dark Lords of the Sith on the planet Korriban. Tuk'ata were unusually intelligent and were even rumoured to communicate with one another through means unknown. It was claimed that originally the species were non-violent grazing animals before being corrupted by Sith alchemy experiments that awakened latent p

creatures.label: chrysalide rancor
creatures.desc: The chrysalide (also known as the "chrysalis beast" or "chrysalide rancor"), was a creature created from rancors and altered by Sith alchemy. It was widely believed that during ancient times, the knowledge of creating the chrysalis beast was formed by the ancient Sith race. In those early years, the creatures served the Sith Empire as pets or protectors to high-ranking officers or powerful nobles.

creatures.label: ikee

evidence.why: venom/poison damage capacity (common; counts as a weak signal only)

creatures.desc: A single great eye walking on soft tentacles, warm to the touch and blind to nothing. The clans keep them because an ikee sees the glint of buried metal long before a Jawa does - and because a people known across the desert by their own glowing eyes cannot help but read one as a good omen. It eats what the waste offers.

creatures.desc: The Empress Butterfly originates from an extremely rare type of planet – a Paradise Glitterworld. These planets have reached an extreme level of technology, but their inhabitants are very psychically sensitive, using their technology to offset any impact they might have on the planet's ecosystem and thereby anima. The Empress Butterfly was engineered as the perfect pollinator, gathering pollen fro

creatures.label: skiphound
creatures.desc: The concept behind the creation of Skiphounds was conceptually simple: DNA from an Animus Vox spliced into the genome of loyal companion dogs to create a creature that could always come when called, being capable of psionically detecting the wishes of its master. The result, however, was completely unexpected: Skiphounds uncontrollably use their latent psionic powers to "blink" in and out of exist

creatures.label: maligoat
creatures.desc: Naturally so hideous and maligned for its looks that it makes people flinch and cringe on sight, it is not often kept as a farm animal. For those that do so however, it produces milk of a high quality not seen elsewhere.

creatures.label: red-horned larpah
creatures.desc:
An elusive and deceitful creature, the red-horned larpah is a large leporidae with tall brown antlers protruding from it's head. While it may look gentle, larpah's apperence belies its predatory, fierce nature. As they grow older, a thick layer of dried blood from past battles coats their horns, earning them the moniker of "red-horned".

Deadly and tough for its size, its aggressiveness rarely dis

runs an effecter on nearby pawns
custom AI think tree <VEF_AnimalWeirdEater> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc:
This strange looking crustacean was created with a single goal in mind: mineral processing. The Terramorph can feed on iron compounds, and process them chemically to slowly turn them into a hardened mineral usually know as "sky steel", that is normally only found in asteroids.

The transmutation process is very slow, so the Terramorph needs to spend quite a lot of time surrounded by mined Steel lu

creatures.label: bearcat
creatures.desc:
Massive, fluffy murder babies is just one of the many “cute” nicknames made for this animal, their only downside being that they’re unable to purr. Because they’re so large, they often end up knocking over the people they’re trying to show affection to before laying on top of them for warmth.

An ursine hybrid with recessive feline genes. Retaining their intelligence and being faster and more fier

detonates in a big explosion when killed

creatures.desc:
A huge, floating gelatinous creature. Propelled by the hydrogen it collects from water and various plant matter, these squishy creatures wander the lands, aimlessly bouncing off objects in their path. One of the few rare creatures around here that strangely isn’t out for human blood. Well, isn’t that nice?

This Aerofleet has somehow grown to extreme size. A small number of younger Aerofleets seem
