creatures.desc:
A general all-rounder vehicle, the Wagon performs well in all categories with a good cargo and passenger capacity. Best suited on flat roads and will struggle somewhat on hills, snow or winter tiles.

Similar to other tier 2 vehicles, this has double fuel efficiency on the world map which makes them more efficient than tier 1 vehicles. They are also less visible due to improved manufacturing.

<co

creatures.label: Wisent
creatures.desc:
A military-grade all-purpose transporter, the Wisent is a powerful truck capable of transporting both plentiful cargo and soldiers into hostile territory. Terrible fuel economy, however it can quickly navigate through rough terrain.

Counter to other tier 2 vehicles, this is less efficient but more effective when travelling away from roads. Passengers sitting in the back will be exposed to enemy f

creatures.label: legate
creatures.desc: An ultraheavy mech with a built-in advanced shield bubble generator. The Legate lacks the point-defense bulb turret present in Centurions, but in exchange it is armed with a super heavy charge blaster that is much more dangerous than standard ones.

creatures.label: furpotamus
creatures.desc:
Furpotamus are colossal, fur-covered ancestors of modern hippos, adapted to wetlands, swamps and cold riverbanks. Despite their heavy bodies, they move easily through flooded terrain and become far more dangerous near water.

They are herbivores, but territorial when harmed or pressured. Domestication is possible, though difficult due to their size, appetite and grazing needs. Hunters seek them fo

creatures.label: centurion
creatures.desc: An ultraheavy mech with a built-in shield bubble generator. The centurion carries a point-defense bulb turret capable of firing while the mechanoid is moving.

creatures.label: nociosphere

evidence.why: applies a hediff to everything in an aura
custom AI think tree <Nociosphere> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc:
A dark metallic sphere covered with curved and jagged grooves. The sphere emanates sensations of pain. It hurts to be near it.

The sphere thrums with a mysterious energy. It appears to be increasing in activity. It's not clear what will happen when it reaches its full capacity. However, if you capture it, you can decrease its activity by suppressing it.

creatures.label: abyssal colo
creatures.desc: A deep-trench morph of the colo, spotted in rows of blue bioluminescence that it can dim to nothing. It hunts in full dark below the silt line, where a lamp is not a tool but an invitation.

creatures.label: Plastemmoth
creatures.recReason: tusks and shaggy coat, plus spines
creatures.desc:
Plastemmoths are colossal biometallic beasts that roam frozen and temperate regions. Their strength, resilience and body mass make them one of the most dangerous hunts on the frontier, especially when encountered moving with other members of the herd.

Over a lifetime, plastite formations slowly grow within the body, shaped by biological processes and extreme environmental pressure. These unstable

creatures.label: teramantis

evidence.why: can be drafted like a colonist
custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: An incredibly rare and monstrously large insectoid of the Chelis geneline, the teramantis is the formidable leader of insectoid hives on the steppe planets of Chelis. Known as a prime male, this massive insectoid is equipped with lethal ripper claws sharp enough to cleave armored vehicles in two. Complementing its fearsome offensive capabilities, the teramantis boasts a large set of wings, grantin

creatures.label: demolisher

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: The strange demolisher mechanoid looks like a weird amalgamation of a deep sea crab, a star-nosed mole and an armoured combat vehicle. Demolishers are armed with a very dangerous short range turret that fires demolisher charges, capable of blowing up even the strongest walls in two or three hits. Once they have ruptured a colony's outer defenses, their enormous plasteel reinforced claws can make s

creatures.label: infernus
creatures.desc: An ultra-heavy mechanoid with an incredibly dangerous orbital strike targeter. The targeter won't cause any damage on its own, but a devastating orbital strike will be launched a few seconds after it finishes focusing on a target. This attack takes a long time to charge, and it has a large minimum range. The Infernus accumulates heat constantly due to its enormous size, and it can release it to ig

creatures.label: siegebreaker
creatures.desc: The siegebreaker is a particularly dangerous tank-shaped mechanoid. Armed with a Siegebreaker Cannon that fires explosive shells, they can detect a hostile presence from hundreds of meters away, acting as unrelenting siege weapons that can obliterate even the strongest defense. Their movement is incredibly slow, and their cannon takes a very long time to recharge, but they should be treated as pri

creatures.label: siegemelter
creatures.desc: The siegemelter is a variant of the siegebreaker armed with a powerful flamethrower. Their movement is incredibly slow, but their siegemelter turret has a considerable range, so they should be treated as priority targets in most cases.

creatures.label: starfire
creatures.desc: The Starfire mechanoid is a massive tank-like machine, equipped with a powerful cannon that fires very slow-moving unstable singularities. These singularities are generated by a complex fusion reactor at the heart of the machine, which channels and amplifies energy from nearby stars via microscopic skipgates. When fired, the singularities unleash devastating amounts of energy, capable of obliterat

creatures.label: bantha cart
creatures.desc:
Two banthas and a two-wheeled cart. Nothing on this world moves more weight for less trouble, and nothing looks less impressive doing it.

A bantha is a mountain of shaggy hide under a pair of spiral horns, and it is stupid in the specific way that makes an animal useful — it will lean into a load until the load moves or the harness breaks, and it does not form an opinion about which. They eat any

creatures.label: chalicotherium
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Despite what its bizzare appearance could suggest, chalicotherium is most closely related to horses and rhinoceroses.
It walks on its knuckles and uses its huge sloth-like claws as both a rake and a mean of defense against predators.

creatures.label: goldilox
creatures.desc:
Tales are told of a gleaming giant gilding the very earth it walks upon, making a king out of the poorest serf with the treasure left in its wake. Many such myths surround the fabled goldilox, a legendary beast who roams the world. While peaceful by nature, goldilox is a fierce defender, trampling any who incur its wrath beneath golden hooves.

The few who ever managed to tame the beast were rewar

creatures.label: devourer

evidence.why: swallows a pawn whole and digests it
custom AI think tree <Devourer> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: A massive monster with a gaping toothed maw and a stubby, snake-like body. The devourer can leap several times its body length to swallow a person whole. Powerful stomach acids rapidly digest the still-living victim. The remains are regurgitated soon after.

creatures.label: mecha-horse

evidence.why: dies unless its genetic timer is reset
mech hybrid — answers a mech antenna

creatures.desc:
More machine than horse, the mecha-horse has an agile frame covered by ablative panels. Though well-liked by riders for its speed and agility, it has a significant design flaw: it heats up considerably during extended travels, needing to periodically vent excess heated air generated on their internal machinery.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color>Mechanoid hybrids are always created with a con

creatures.label: thrumboman

evidence.why: humanoid hybrid — works like a colonist

creatures.desc:
Look, we know what you want, a thrumbo that won’t eat your crops before they’ve harvested, thereby wasting entire seasons of growth for your most valuable plants. And we’re here to tell you it doesn’t exist. But we’ve gotten close in that this one will typically harvest your plants before it eats them for worse nutritional gain. Unless it’s trees, in which case we got nothing.

A colossal hybrid w

creatures.desc:

A vicious dromaeosaurid that takes down prey via deadly lunge attacks. Known for practically infesting many of the abandoned facilities on Sorna during the 1997 incident, resembling Velociraptor sornaensis in appearence. When Masrani corp. acquired InGen, the design of the Deinonychus was altered quite sign

creatures.label: Dracorex
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #032119-2006 [DRACOREX HOGWARTSIA] CODENAME: DRAGON-KING >781

A strange pachycephalosaurid with a flat crest atop its head, decorated in sharp spines. Despite its fearsome appearence, they are quite gentle.

creatures.label: Dromaeosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #045644-1922 [DROMAEOSAURUS ALBERTENSIS] CODENAME: RUNNER >482

A quick moving dromaeosaur with razor sharp teeth and long, sickle like claws ready for shredding. Their mottled hides allow them to run through tall grasses and blend well into the shadows of the foliage before the pack moves in for the kill. Despite having a rugged build compared to other dromaeosaurs,

creatures.label: Gallimimus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #09922-1972 [GALLIMIMUS BULLATUS] CODENAME: BULLET >445

A speedy omnivorous ornithomimid, the largest of its kind discovered. They have been observed engaging in flocking behaviour when danger is nearby. Don't get in their way.

creatures.label: Homalocephale
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #093627-1974 [HOMALOCEPHALE CALATHOCERCOS] CODENAME: VALENTINE >4

A small and generally docile pachycephalosaurid with a flat, heart shaped head. They can be seen gathering in large family herds for protection as they forage.

creatures.label: Oviraptor
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #038292-1924 [OVIRAPTOR PHILOCERATOPS] CODENAME: KLEPTO >6

A nimble, scrawny theropod that loves shiny things and unwanted debris. If given an inch, they'll even steal the clothes off your back.

A pachycephalosaurid with a thick dome and a mottled cream and blue hide. Their calls have made them a nuisance, so much so small tribal villages will actively ward them away, lest they attract larger threats.

creatures.desc:

[TROODON PECTINODON]

WOUNDING TOOTH

Bred on Isla Sorna during the initial testing phase of Jurassic Park, Troodon were considered to be too dangerous for public display, and were ordered to be destroyed. Dangerous and deadly, this dinosaur has caused much chaos and claimed many casualities in InGens earth history regarding several incidents over a span of many years. They are smart, have the ability to think, solve cognitive hazards, and are the one thing you do not want to meet face to face. The other

creatures.label: grondrak
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest rodent of all time, josephoartigasia, resembles a gigantic capybara or pacarana, but in a few regards it appears to be closer to today's hippopotamuses.
It is not a very good runner, and to compensate for that, it sports huge incisors that could prove very dangerous to lesser predators.

creatures.label: king toad

evidence.why: mod wrote custom C# pawn class
custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc: While a normal giant frog will rarely reach a 30 year lifespan, their gene code does allow 1 in 10000 to undergo a mutation that functionally stops their aging. Those toads will grow in size, power and appetite until one day earning the name of King Toad, a stoic mountain in the skin of an amphibian, swallowing its prey whole and leaving nothing behind. They are just as fast as their smaller breth

creatures.label: dunbear
creatures.desc:
Dunbears are ancient cave bears of monumental size, adapted to extreme cold and mountainous regions. They spend long periods in deep hibernation, waking with the thaw to roam the surface in search of food.

Hunting a Dunbear is a dangerous decision. Its mass, resilience and brute strength let it survive wounds that would drop most predators, while its dense and valuable fur makes it a tempting pri

creatures.label: diabolus
creatures.desc:
An ultra-heavy mechanoid with an ultra-powerful hellsphere cannon. Made for siegebreaking, its hellsphere cannon takes time to charge up a shot, but can melt concrete and vaporize bone. The diabolus dissipates the hellsphere cannon's waste power in a heat column mounted on its back, which can pulse to ignite flammable objects nearby.

This mech's name comes from a thousand-year-old poem written by

creatures.label: war queen
creatures.desc:
An ultra-heavy mech with a built-in mech gestator. Fed with appropriate resources, the war queen can form small war urchin combat mechs within its massive carapace and deploy them into combat.

Even more than other mechanoids, the war queen resembles a giant, living insect. All war mechs can be terrifying, but humans tend to find the war queen disturbing on a deeper level.

creatures.label: woolly stegosaurus
creatures.desc:
A variation of the more common “roof lizard”, this creature is a herbivore characterized by their distinctive kite-shaped upright bony scales along the back which help regulate their body temperature and acts as a mating display.

The Woolly Stegosaurus finds their home in cold biomes, preferring to eat low-lying vegetation due to a short neck and small head. The spines on the end of the tail diff

creatures.label: thrumbo
creatures.desc:
A gigantic, graceful creature of unknown origin. The thrumbo is gentle by nature, but extremely dangerous when enraged. While its long fur is exceptionally beautiful, its hide is also incredibly resistant to damage. Its razor-sharp horn fetches a huge price.

Legends say that an old thrumbo is the wisest creature in the universe - it simply chooses not to speak.

creatures.label: toxbear
creatures.desc:
The Toxbear is a monstrous and deadly creature born from a polluted environment. Standing at an immense size, this mutated bear is a force to be reckoned with. With no natural predators, it roams and hunts at will, leaving destruction in its wake. Its aggressive behavior is fueled by cancerous growth around its head, making it nearly impervious to damage.

As the growth puts pressure on its brain,

creatures.label: patriarch

evidence.why: can be drafted like a colonist

creatures.desc: The gargantuan patriarch of the Sorne geneline serves as the primary male responsible for the survival and protection of the royal caste. His immense digger claws, essential for both hive construction and defense, double as formidable shields capable of absorbing extraordinary amounts of damage. Mounted on his back are vast insect jelly sacks, which provide the resources necessary for rapidly cons

creatures.label: titantick

evidence.why: can be drafted like a colonist
produces <Chemfuel> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc: An incredibly rare and monstrously large insectoid of the Nuchadus geneline, the titantick is a formidable engineered tick, designed to serve as a mobile fuel depot on the harsh magma planet of Nuchadus. This creature features an enormous chemfuel sack attached to its lower abdomen, which is prone to leaking vast quantities of fuel when damaged. In addition to its capacity to store fuel, the titan

creatures.label: obbak
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest known marsupial to have ever lived. As huge as a rhinoceros, it resembles a gigantic wombat.
Diprotodon's a relatively peaceful creature, however its huge pair of forward-facing teeth as well as its strong claws can prove quite dangerous in a combat situation.

creatures.label: rock troll

evidence.why: custom damage capacities (modded DamageDef), not plain bite/scratch

creatures.desc:
The rock troll is a colossal, eyeless creature often found living in caves and underground chasms. Much more reclusive than its northern cousins, the rock troll will only surface from its underground lair when provoked.

Lacking regenerative abilities, the rock troll makes up for it through a strange process known as self-petrification. Any open wound will almost immediately be closed by ultra-fas

creatures.label: thrumhorse

evidence.why: can be drafted like a colonist

creatures.desc:
A very nice combination of two highly adaptive baseline creatures which arguably results in the best riding companion man could ask for. While this isn’t apparent in their speed, it definitely is so once a rider experiences the thundering beats of this horsey positively barreling through entire forests and marshland in order to earn its next sugar cube the size of a fist.

A colossal hybrid with r

creatures.label: Enigmosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #06380-1983 [ENIGMOSAURUS MONGOLIENSIS] CODENAME: RIDDLE >592

A therizinosauroid theropod covered in short, downy fuzz similar to that of an emu. Their name derives from the unusual shape of the hip bone due to the fact that, at the time of discovery, there was little known about therizinosauroids. Their sharp claws are well suited to slicing branches and crushing sm

creatures.label: Saltasaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #099362-1985 [SALTASAURUS TITUSI] CODENAME: PEBBLESTONE >5

A large sauropod covered in knobbly osteoderms. These greatly improve defense alongside its humongous side and strength.

creatures.label: Segnosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #04938-1979 [SEGNOSAURUS GALBINENSIS] CODENAME: VEGAS >932

A therizinosauroid theropod covered in multicoloured feathers. creatures.label: Therizinosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #04233-1954 [THERIZINOSAURUS CHELONIFORMIS] CODENAME: RAKE >482

A large  maniraptoran theropod dinosaur that boasts incredible, scythe like claws on each hand. Despite their fearsome appearence, these dinosaurs are actually herbivores, though that doesn't make them any less deadly when angry and provoked. Much of this creatures skeleton is still left to be discoverd,

creatures.label: mastodon
creatures.desc: A massive elephant-like mammal. While briefly extinct, the mastodon now roams countless worlds due to its resilience to bitter cold. Its thick hide makes excellent cold-weather clothing. However, hunting the animal is a dangerous proposition even for skilled hunters.

creatures.label: megalochelys
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest tortoise of all time.
There aren't many predators that pose a threat to megalochelys, thanks to its thick and hard as rock shell. The ones that attempt to attack it anyway, will have to be prepared to deal with its surprisingly powerful bite.

creatures.label: rannak
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

One of the largest, if not the largest bear in history. What stands out the most about its appearance is the disproportionately short snout compared to other bears and the extraordinarily long legs it possesses. The latter makes it so hardly any prey can effectively outrun it.

creatures.label: Bulldog
creatures.desc:
A general main battle tank, the Bulldog is an improved combat vehicle that performs well in any engagement. Performs better in less favourable terrain with all sides armoured, the thinnest plating being at the rear near the engine.

Different to other tier 2 vehicles, this has regular fuel efficiency and is quite visible, which is still an improvement over the tier 1 tank.

<color=#bb8f04>Crew:</c

creatures.label: Tango
creatures.desc:
A general purpose armoured personnel carrier, the Tango is a slow but hardy troop transport. Ample cargo holds, hardened armour, all-terrain capability and a turret that can fire either mobile or stationary, the main downside is fuel consumption and slightly thinner plating on the rear.

Different to other tier 2 vehicles, this has regular fuel efficiency and is quite visible, its high fuel consum

creatures.label: war empress
creatures.desc: An ultra-heavy mech with a built-in mech gestator. Fed with appropriate resources, the War empress can form swarms of small melee-adept guttersnipe combat mechs within its massive carapace and deploy them into combat. The Empress is armed with a very dangerous and long ranged slug sniper turret that should be avoided at all costs, but the greatest threat comes from her sharp rending claws, which s

creatures.label: Balloon
creatures.desc:
A lighter-than-air aircraft consisting of a bag, called an envelope, which contains heated air. Suspended beneath is a wicker basket which carries passengers and a source of heat.

<color=#bb8f04>Crew:</color> Driver x1, Passenger x1
<color=#bb8f04>Fuel type:</color> Wood

<color=#bb8f04>Pedantry PSA:</color> I know hot air balloons don't use ballast. I don't care, it looks cool. Plus this one use

creatures.label: krondar
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

This mysterious carnivore was the biggest predatory mammal of its time.
Often described as a "bear-dog", it was apparently related to entelodonts, hippopotamuses, and whales.

creatures.label: dreadmeld

custom AI think tree <Fleshbeast> — it does not behave like an animal

Fleshbeast dreadmelds are rarely seen above ground, instead sheltering in caverns built from living flesh. They share a psychic connection with the flesh used to create their burrow.

creatures.label: Ankylosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #02817-1908 [ANKYLOSAURUS MAGNIVENTRIS] CODENAME: CHURCHILL >25

A strong, armour plated ankylosaurid with a distinct clubbed tail. Many skulls have been crushed thanks to the sheer force it wields.

creatures.label: Antarctopelta
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #02817-1986 [ANTARCTOPELTA OLIVEROI] CODENAME: T-28 >95

An odd ankylosaurid with a slender form and large, curved spikes. What it lacks in brute strength it makes up for in tenacity.

creatures.label: Camptosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #07183-1885 [CAMPTOSAURUS DISPAR] CODENAME: FLEX >37

A docile ornithischian with a spotty hide. Their beak has thick ridges along the inside to help with shredding plant matter - and for nipping curious colonists.

creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #09383-2010 [COAHUILACERATOPS MAGNACUERNA] CODENAME: MARIGOLD >70

A bulky chasmosaurine ceratopsian that has integrated well into the harsh life on the rim. The markings on their frill have proven effective at scaring predators away.

An extinct genus related to the modern day alligator. With its powerful jaws this creature is able to take down dinosaurs with ease, drowning and tearing their victims apart after ambushing them from the water below.

creatures.label: Edmontosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #0883-1940 [EDMONTOSAURUS REGALIS] CODENAME: CAMO >382

A striped hadrosaurid with a bellowing call. They are heavyset, more so than other hadrosaurs, and use this to their advantage in combat.

creatures.label: ssgrondak
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #038723-1858 [ESTEMMENOSUCHUS MIRABILIS] CODENAME: CROWN >829

A bizarre omnivorous synapsid that sports a pair of peculiar antlers atop its head. While not particularly aggressive these creatures can pack a powerful bite, and gore small creatures to death.

creatures.label: Indominus rex
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #???-???
[INDOMINUS REX]

THE UNTAMABLE KING

Boasting superior intellect, an incredibly high prey drive and claws and teeth made for rendering flesh, the Indominus rex is a dangerous, terrifying foe to face out on the battlefield. Their ivory hides are marked with scars and cuts from many countless battles, and their roar invokes fear in all that hear it. The Indomin

creatures.label: Indoraptor
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #???-??? [INDORAPTOR]

THE INDOMITABLE THIEF

Posessing amazing intelligent capabilities and the ability to process and follow orders, the Indoraptor was built to be the ultimate machine in combat. Their razor sharp claws allow them slice through skin and bone, their jaws boasting incredible strength, as well as the ability to echolocate. The Indominus genome was supp

creatures.label: Kentrosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03728-1915 [KENTROSAURUS AETHIOPICUS] CODENAME: SPEAR >369

A 'primitive' stegosaurian dinosaur that sports a deadly tail covered in spikes. While not quick to turn, these dinosaurs have often wielded their tails efficiently in combat, slicing and piercing attackers.

creatures.label: Kosmoceratops
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #07822-2010 [KOSMOCERATOPS RICHARDSONI] CODENAME: ORNAMENT >777

A chasmosaurine ceratopsian with an incredible display frill on their crest. Known amusingly as 'the horniest dinosaur ever discovered' they have a whopping fifteen horn like structures on their face.

creatures.label: Mochlodon
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #09372-1871 [MOCHLODON GOBIENSIS] CODENAME: SUNSET >432

An iguanodontid with an orange hide. They can be found wandering in small herds searching for new grazing grounds.

creatures.label: Nasutoceratops
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #013729-1985 [NASUTOCERATOPS TITUSI] CODENAME: EL-TAURO >5

A hardy ceratopsian with two forward facing horns and a large snout. Their powerful horns can skewer threats with ease.

creatures.label: ssvarrak
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03093-1976 [OURANOSAURUS NIGERIENSIS] CODENAME: DAWN >3722

A beautiful hadrosaur with an orange crest, rising like the sun over the hillbanks. They are skittish but generally docile.

creatures.label: Pachyrhinosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03453-1950 [PACHYRHINOSAURUS CANADENSIS] CODENAME: THICK-NOSE >4721

A centrosaurine ceratopsid with a thick, chubby nose and an intricate display frill. Fossil sites discovered prove that these dinosaurs looked after their young as a herd.

creatures.label: Parasaurolophus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #02839-1922 [PARASAUROLOPHUS WALKERI] CODENAME: NEAR-CREST >3228

An ornithopod dinosaur that walked in both a quadrupedal and bipedal stance. They are perhaps one of the most well known hadrosaurs.

creatures.label: Rhabdodon
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #02321-1869 [RHABDODON PRISCUS] CODENAME: FLUTE >872

A large ornithopod with a green hide and crimson stripes. A very prominent herbivore, they are seen congregating in large groups as they graze, keeping an eye out for danger.

creatures.label: Sarcosuchus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03829-1966 [SARCOSUCHUS IMPERATOR] CODENAME: BEARTRAP >082

A humongous crocodyliform with an elongated snout and a extremely powerful bite. Several rows of razor sharp teeth allow this creature to shred unsuspecting prey to pieces before sending them to a watery grave.

creatures.label: Scutosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03812-1922 [SCUTOSAURUS KARPINSKII] CODENAME: SHIELD >082

A peculiar pareiasaur with elongated spikes growing down from their chin. They are bulky, quite lumberous, and are dimwitted, but quite charming, in an odd way.

creatures.label: Stegosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03729-1887 [STEGOSAURUS STENOPS] CODENAME: THYREOS >230

A very famous stegosaurid. They are protective over their young, but are often very forgiving of intruders to their stomping grounds, unless they pose a threat. They wield their tail deftly.

creatures.label: Styracosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #039902-1913 [STYRACOSAURUS ALBERTENSIS] CODENAME: STYRAX >230

A ceratopsian well known for the multitude of spikes decorating its head. Smaller than most ceratopsians, they often use their lesser stature for speed rather than strength.

creatures.label: Tenontosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #02321-1970 [TENONTOSAURUS TILLETTI] CODENAME: SINEW >412

A large ornithopod with a slender, elongated tail, theorized to have acted as a whip with which it attacked predators, or perhaps other unruly herd members. They are often preyed upon by dinosaurs which hunt in packs.

creatures.label: ssborrak
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #0481-1891 [TOROSAURUS LATUS] CODENAME: PERFORATE >732

A small ceratopsian with a slender, almost flat frill. Recent studies suggest that it and Triceratops horridus are perhaps the same creature, leaving the genus dubious, but valid, for now.

creatures.label: Triceratops
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #0481-1889 [TRICERATOPS HORRIDUS] CODENAME: TRINITY >526

An extremely famous ceratopsid dinosaur. Noble and proud, these incredible forces of nature have stood the test of time and intregrated well into the rim. They are well known for their bravery, and their supposed rivalry with Tyrannosaurus rex.

creatures.label: Zalmoxes
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #05541-1899 [ZALMOXES ROBUSTUS] CODENAME: HERODOTUS >532

A small ornithopod with a bright orange hide that almost sparkles. They are quick and highly strung but generally quite peaceful. Their leather has become quite sought after within certain tribes.

creatures.label: vhorbantha
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Very close relatives of modern elephants. Hunted by early humans for their meat, fur, and valuable tusks. 
As opposed to their today's equivalents, the mammoths' ears and tails are relatively short - to minimise frostbite and heat loss.

creatures.label: deinotherium
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

"Deinotherium" means "terrible beast". It's a unique cousin to mammoths and mastodons, equipped with downward curving tusks on the lower jaw.
Very short-tempered and incredibly dangerous when angered.

creatures.label: boomnotherium

evidence.why: produces <VCHE_Deepchem> — not a normal animal product

creatures.desc:
The Boomnotherium is an hybrid between a boomalope and a large prehistoric relative of modern-day elephants. In latin, boomnotherium roughly translates as "terrible beast that will explode in your ass".

Useful abilities: Boomnotheriums produce huge amounts of chemfuel, and they are "tanky", able to withstand a lot of abuse before exploding.

creatures.label: Smuggler
creatures.desc:
A general-purpose aircraft, the Smuggler is an extremely fast and effective mode of transportation. While it is faster and can carry more cargo than helicopters, it requires a landing strip to both take off and land.

Different to other tier 2 vehicles, this has regular fuel efficiency on the world map but moves significantly faster in return.

Being a flying vehicle, it is extremely obvious when

creatures.label: Acrocanthosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #038292-1950 [ACROCANTHOSAURUS ATOKENSIS] CODENAME: MIDAS >9

A large, dangerous theropod with golden skin. Its incredibly powerful bite can tear the flesh of a colonist apart like a hot knife through butter.

creatures.label: Allosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #08822-1877 [ALLOSAURUS FRAGILIS] CODENAME: NEMEAN >27

A large, blood red theropod with a distinctly curved neck. They are known to sport a very foul temper once provoked.

creatures.label: Apatosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #01829-1887 [APATOSAURUS AJAX] CODENAME: TITAN >71

A well-known sauropod with no real distinguishing features. It is large and hardy, even more so when travelling in herds.

creatures.label: Argentinosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #09382-1993 [ARGENTINOSAURUS HUINCULENSIS] CODENAME: COLOSSUS >65

A humongous sauropod with emerald skin. It is an incredible force of nature, able to crush predators under their weight with disgusting ease.

creatures.label: ssorrbantha
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03827-1903 [BRACHIOSAURUS ALTITHORAX] CODENAME: ATLAS >90

A colossal sauropod that towers above all else, their neck reaching up to the heavens. They are powerful creatures that are not to be trifled with, their strength greater than that of many carnivores.

creatures.label: Camarasaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #0928-1877 [CAMARASAURUS SUPREMUS] CODENAME: CHAMBER >20

A stocky sauropod that has a soothing call. While not massive or all too powerful, they are still capable of fending for themselves if need be. Gentle when unprovoked.

creatures.label: Carcharodontosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #02983-1925 [CARCHARODONTOSAURUS SAHARICUS] CODENAME: JAGGED >37

A large theropod with pitch black skin. They have become infamous with local tribes due to their ferocity, dubbed the 'Black Death', a name whispered in hushed fear between hunters.

creatures.label: Giganotosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #09546-1995 [GIGANOTOSAURUS CAROLINII] CODENAME: WRATH >593

A remarkably sized theropod often described as one of the largest known terrestrial predators. With an incredible bite force, teeth for slicing flesh and the ability to sprint large distances at quite the speed, this predator is one to be feared. Gigantosaurus are thankfully solitary creatures for most of th

creatures.label: Spinosaurus
creatures.recReason: sail back and croc snout, famous
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #07642-1915 [SPINOSAURUS AEGYPTIACUS] CODENAME: SOBEK >482

An extremely large theropod with a sail running along its back. Viscious and incredibly deadly, this creature was bred illegally and wreaked havoc during the 2001 incident on Isla Sorna.

creatures.label: Supersaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #03927-1985 [SUPERSAURUS VIVIANAE] CODENAME: MONUMENT >908

A beautiful sauropod with a jade-like hide. Gathering in large herds, these massive creatures spend the majority of the day grazing to sate their hearty appetite.

creatures.label: Tyrannosaurus rex
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #09182-1905[TYRANNOSAURUS REX] CODENAME: KING >1

The king tyrant lizard. Boasting incredible power, tenacity and speed, this dinosaur has earned its namesake. It was responsible for much chaos on the mainland of San Fransico during the 1997 incident, where it was revealed it had wreaked havoc prior on Isla Nublar during 1994.

creatures.label: Yangchuanosaurus
creatures.desc:
-- > INGEN INTERNAL CASE FILE #0498-1978 [YANGCHUANOSAURUS SHANGYOUENSIS] CODENAME: LAZULI >472

A metriacanthosaurid theropod with a spotty blue hide. They are a fierce predator, their huge size allowing them to overpower many different species of prey.

creatures.label: bulwark

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <HiveMind> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: A massive and lumbering alien beast capable of rending steel and biting through concrete. It is EXTREMELY dangerous and is best dealt with using explosives and AT weapons, or better-yet landmines.

creatures.label: Warbird
creatures.desc:
A general-purpose fighter plane, the Warbird is an incredibly fast and effective attack craft. With minimal cargo intended for holding maintenance equipment and fuel, its primary purpose is to engage other aircraft and initiate strafing manoeuvres.

Different to other tier 2 vehicles, this has regular fuel efficiency on the world map but moves significantly faster in return.

Being a flying vehicl

creatures.label: mechathrumbo

evidence.why: dies unless its genetic timer is reset
mech hybrid — answers a mech antenna

creatures.desc:
This hulking cybernetic behemoth is why you don't need tanks in the Rim. Its huge plasteel carapace hides a miniaturized synchrotron that constantly generates small amounts of antimatter, which is instantly used to fill a miniature antigrain warhead. Slow, but quite effective.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color>Mechanoid hybrids are always created with a controller booster, making the mechath

creatures.label: sskorrath
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

Quite possibly, the largest crocodilian of all time, and also the biggest reptile to roam the Earth after the extinction of dinosaurs.
It is so massive that even giant ground sloths have a place on its menu.

creatures.label: sserrakoth
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The second biggest snake in history, thought to have been the largest until the discovery of titanoboa.
It much prefers hunting big animals as they're easier to smell out.

creatures.label: storm sando
creatures.desc: A pelagic morph, blue-striped with bioluminescence and finned for open water rather than trench. Faster than the grey, ranging the upper column where it attacks from above like weather. Sailors call the first sign of one "the sky going out".

creatures.label: ssorrakoth
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant reptiles, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest snake ever discovered, Titanoboa, is capable of swallowing cows whole. It can kill even medium-sized animals in just seconds, and thus should be stayed away from at all costs.

creatures.label: mecha-muffalo

evidence.why: dies unless its genetic timer is reset
mech hybrid — answers a mech antenna

creatures.desc:
This hulking cybernetic organism has been reinforced with an adaptive plasteel mesh, enabling it to carry an incredible amount of stuff. The mecha-muffalo is the perfect pack animal, but it is quite useless in an offensive role. Defensively, however, it is armed with a smoke cannon that it can use to cover the battlefield in a dense cloud of dust.

<color=#E5E54C>Gameplay effect:</color> Mechanoid

creatures.label: brood lord

evidence.why: custom AI think tree <HiveMind> — it does not behave like an animal

creatures.desc: A massive and lumbering alien beast capable of rending steel and biting through concrete. It is EXTREMELY dangerous and is best dealt with using explosives and AT weapons, or better-yet landmines.

creatures.label: sando aqua monster
creatures.desc: The apex of the Naboo core: a grey, lion-faced swimming quadruped the length of a cargo hauler, mammalian and warm-blooded and utterly unhurried. It takes colo claw fish the way a diver takes a ration bar. There is always a bigger fish; this is it.

creatures.label: paraceratherium
creatures.desc:
Long extinct giant mammals, brought back to life as a part of the Megafauna Project.

The largest land mammal known to man, Paraceratherium, is a gentle creature, however its size alone can also make it quite a formidable foe to face.
Feeds on plants and trees, which it can easily reach with its extraordinarily long neck, the trait that makes it unique to other genera of rhinoceroses.

creatures.label: archocentipede

evidence.why: produces <ComponentIndustrial> — not a normal animal product
can be drafted like a colonist

creatures.desc: The Archocentipede is the end result of the Archotech Project, aiming to provide a "friendly" machine superintelligence with a capable body. Even though this centipede is forcefully loyal to the colonists, and can be somewhat controlled by them, most other inhabitants of the planet will consider its existence to be an abomination, since dabbling in archotech usually signals the end of comprehensib

creatures.label: elder sando
creatures.desc: A scarred bull sando, barnacle-crusted, carrying old harpoon wounds it has outlived by a century. One per sea, if that. Named by every crew that has seen it and survived, which is how it came to have so many names.

creatures.label: reefback
creatures.desc: So old the reef grows on it: coral, kelp, a hundred hangers-on that never leave. A moving ecosystem, and the one place in the deep where a crew can rest in the light of something else's garden — as long as nobody puts a harpoon in the garden.

creatures.label: starmaw
creatures.desc: A filter-feeder the size of a hull, spotted in bioluminescent patterns that read like a night sky when it rises. Sailors navigate by it, and by the crews that vanished trying to.

creatures.label: lanternwhale
creatures.desc: Moss-shrouded and trailing blue lantern tendrils that draw the plankton it strains, the lanternwhale is the largest living thing in the seas. It does not notice you. That is the whole of its character, until you make it.

creatures.label: the Long Hunger
creatures.recReason: not a creature silhouette at all
creatures.desc: The ground here is not empty by chance. Something vast lives beneath the dunes, drawn by vibration and gone again within the hour - and it has been swallowing whatever the desert offers it for longer than any settlement's records go back.
